16.206.m: Then that which is the fifth division of the day is remembered as evening. (96)

16.206.s:
.. tathā ca śrutiḥ .. ..
yadaivādityo'tha vasanto yadā saṃgaviko'tha grīṣmo yadā vā mādhyaṃdino'tha varṣā yadaparāhṇo'tha śarat ..
ghadevāstametyatha hemanta iti .. 97 ..
16.206.d:
.. तथा च श्रुतिः .. ..
यदैवादित्योऽथ वसन्तो यदा संगविकोऽथ ग्रीष्मो यदा वा माध्यंदिनोऽथ वर्षा यदपराह्णोऽथ शरत् ..
घदेवास्तमेत्यथ हेमन्त इति .. 97 ..
16.206.m: And likewise the Śruti says: / 'When the sun rises, that is spring; when it is saṃgava, that is summer; when it is midday, that is the rainy season; when it is afternoon, that is autumn; / when it sets, that is winter.' (97)

16.206.s:
prārabhya kutape śrāddhe kuryādārohaṇaṃ budhaḥ ..
vidhijño vidhimāsthāya rohiṇaṃ na tu laṃghayet .. 98 ..
16.206.d:
प्रारभ्य कुतपे श्राद्धे कुर्यादारोहणं बुधः ..
विधिज्ञो विधिमास्थाय रोहिणं न तु लंघयेत् .. 98 ..
16.206.m: Having begun the ancestral rite in the kutapa period, the wise man, / adhering to the rules and knowing the rite, should proceed to the ascent, but must not transgress the rohiṇa period. (98)

16.206.s:
aṣṭamo yo muhūrtaśca kutapaḥ sa nigadyate ..
navamo rauhiṇaḥ prokta iti śrāddhavido viduḥ .. 99 ..
16.206.d:
अष्टमो यो मुहूर्तश्च कुतपः स निगद्यते ..
नवमो रौहिणः प्रोक्त इति श्राद्धविदो विदुः .. 99 ..
16.206.m: The eighth muhūrta is called kutapa; / the ninth is declared to be rauhiṇa: so know those who know the ancestral rites. (99)

16.206.s:
ekoddiṣṭaṃ tu madhyāhnaṃ prātarvai jātakarmaṇi ..
pitryārthaṃ nirvapetpākaṃ vaiśvadevārthameva ca .. 7.1.206.100 ..
16.206.d:
एकोद्दिष्टं तु मध्याह्नं प्रातर्वै जातकर्मणि ..
पित्र्यार्थं निर्वपेत्पाकं वैश्वदेवार्थमेव च .. 7.1.206.100 ..
16.206.m: The rite for a single deceased is at midday; in the morning for the birth rite. / One should cook the food separately for the ancestors and for the Vaiśvadeva rite. (100)

16.206.s:
vaiśvadeve na pitryārthaṃ na pitryaṃ vaiśvadevike ..
kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ mahādevi brāhmaṇāṃśca visarjya ca .. 101 ..
16.206.d:
वैश्वदेवे न पित्र्यार्थं न पित्र्यं वैश्वदेविके ..
कृत्वा श्राद्धं महादेवि ब्राह्मणांश्च विसर्ज्य च .. 101 ..
16.206.m: In the Vaiśvadeva rite, what is for the ancestors is not used; in the rite for the ancestors, what is for the Vaiśvadeva is not used. / Having performed the ancestral rite, O great goddess, and having dismissed the brahmins, (101)

16.206.s:
vaiśvadevādikaṃ karma tataḥ kuryādvarānane ..
bahuhavyendhane cāgnau susamiddhe viśeṣataḥ .. 102 ..
16.206.d:
वैश्वदेवादिकं कर्म ततः कुर्याद्वरानने ..
बहुहव्येन्धने चाग्नौ सुसमिद्धे विशेषतः .. 102 ..
16.206.m: one should then perform the rite of Vaiśvadeva and the rest, O fair-faced one, / especially in a fire that has abundant fuel for offerings and is well kindled. (102)

16.206.s:
vidhūme lelihāne ca kuryātkarma prasiddhaye ..
aprabuddhe sadhūme ca juhuyādyo hutāśane .. .. 103 ..
16.206.d:
विधूमे लेलिहाने च कुर्यात्कर्म प्रसिद्धये ..
अप्रबुद्धे सधूमे च जुहुयाद्यो हुताशने .. .. 103 ..
16.206.m: One should perform the rite for success [in a fire that is] smokeless and leaping with flames. / But he who sacrifices into a fire that is not fully kindled and full of smoke,

16.206.s:
yajamāno bhavedandhaḥ kuputra iti niścitam ..
durgandhaścaiva kṛṣṇaśca nīlaścaiva viśeṣataḥ .. 104 ..
16.206.d:
यजमानो भवेदन्धः कुपुत्र इति निश्चितम् ..
दुर्गन्धश्चैव कृष्णश्च नीलश्चैव विशेषतः .. 104 ..
16.206.m: That patron of the sacrifice will become blind, and have a bad son; this is certain. / Especially [fire that is] foul-smelling, black, or blue,

16.206.s:
bhūmiṃ vigāhate yatra tatra vidyātparābhavam ..
arciṣmānpiṃgalaśikhaḥ sarpiḥkāṃcanasaprabhaḥ .. 105 ..
16.206.d:
भूमिं विगाहते यत्र तत्र विद्यात्पराभवम् ..
अर्चिष्मान्पिंगलशिखः सर्पिःकांचनसप्रभः .. 105 ..
16.206.m: And wherever it penetrates into the ground, one should know that defeat will occur there. / Luminous, with yellowish-red flames, possessing the lustre of clarified butter or gold,

16.206.s:
snigdhaḥ pradakṣiṇaścaiva vahniḥ syātkāryasiddhaye ..
aṃjanābhyaṃjanaṃ gaṃdhānmantrapraṇayanaṃ tathā .. 106 ..
16.206.d:
स्निग्धः प्रदक्षिणश्चैव वह्निः स्यात्कार्यसिद्धये ..
अंजनाभ्यंजनं गंधान्मन्त्रप्रणयनं तथा .. 106 ..
16.206.m: Glossy, and curling clockwise—such a fire leads to the success of an undertaking. / Anointing the eyes, rubbing with oil, perfumes, and the bringing of the sacred formula,

16.206.s:
kāśaiḥ punarbhavetkāryaṃ hayamedhaphalaṃ labhet ..
aṣṭajātikapuṣpaṃ ca añjanaṃ nityameva hi .. 107 ..
16.206.d:
काशैः पुनर्भवेत्कार्यं हयमेधफलं लभेत् ..
अष्टजातिकपुष्पं च अञ्जनं नित्यमेव हि .. 107 ..
16.206.m: The ritual should be performed with kāśa grasses; he obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice. / And the jasmine flower (aṣṭajātikā) and collyrium should always be used,

16.206.s:
kṛṣṇebhyaśca tilebhyaśca tailaṃ yatnātsurakṣitam ..
candanāgaruṇī cobhe tamālośīrapadmakam .. 108 ..
16.206.d:
कृष्णेभ्यश्च तिलेभ्यश्च तैलं यत्नात्सुरक्षितम् ..
चन्दनागरुणी चोभे तमालोशीरपद्मकम् .. 108 ..
16.206.m: And oil carefully preserved from black sesamum seeds. / And both sandalwood and agallochum, tamāla, uśīra, and padmaka,

16.206.s:
dhūpaśca gauggulaḥ śreṣṭhastauruṣko dhūpa eva ca ..
śuklāḥ sumanasaḥ śreṣṭhāstathā padmotpalāni ca .. 109 ..
16.206.d:
धूपश्च गौग्गुलः श्रेष्ठस्तौरुष्को धूप एव च ..
शुक्लाः सुमनसः श्रेष्ठास्तथा पद्मोत्पलानि च .. 109 ..
16.206.m: And bdellium incense is the best, as well as olibanum incense. / White fragrant flowers are best, as well as lotuses and water lilies,

16.206.s:
gandhavantyupapannāni yāni cānyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
niśigaṃdhā japā bhiṇḍirūpakaḥ sakuraṃṭakaḥ .. 7.1.206.110 ..
16.206.d:
गन्धवन्त्युपपन्नानि यानि चान्यानि कृत्स्नशः ..
निशिगंधा जपा भिण्डिरूपकः सकुरंटकः .. 7.1.206.110 ..
16.206.m: And whatever other sweet-smelling ones are available, completely. / The night-blooming jasmine, hibiscus, bhindīrūpaka, along with yellow amaranth:

16.206.s:
puṣpāṇi varjanīyāni śrāddhakarmaṇi nityaśaḥ ..
sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ tāmraṃ pitṝṇāṃ pātramucyate .. 111 ..
16.206.d:
पुष्पाणि वर्जनीयानि श्राद्धकर्मणि नित्यशः ..
सौवर्णं राजतं ताम्रं पितॄणां पात्रमुच्यते .. 111 ..
16.206.m: These flowers are always to be avoided in a śrāddha rite. / A vessel of gold, silver, or copper is prescribed for the ancestors.

16.206.s:
rajatasya tathā kiñciddarśanaṃ puṇyadāyakam ..
kṛṣṇājinasya sānnidhyaṃ darśanaṃ dānameva ca .. 112 ..
16.206.d:
रजतस्य तथा किञ्चिद्दर्शनं पुण्यदायकम् ..
कृष्णाजिनस्य सान्निध्यं दर्शनं दानमेव च .. 112 ..
16.206.m: Even a slight sight of silver grants merit. / The presence of a black antelope skin, the sight of it, and indeed the gift of it

16.206.s:
rakṣoghnaṃ caiva varcasyaṃ paśūnputrāṃśca tārayet ..
atha mantraṃ pravakṣyāmi amṛtaṃ brahmanirmitam .. 113 ..
16.206.d:
रक्षोघ्नं चैव वर्चस्यं पशून्पुत्रांश्च तारयेत् ..
अथ मन्त्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि अमृतं ब्रह्मनिर्मितम् .. 113 ..
16.206.m: Destroys demons, promotes vigor, and saves cattle and sons. / Now I will proclaim the nectar-like mantra fashioned by Brahmā:

16.206.s:
devatābhyaḥ pitṛbhyaśca mahāyogibhya eva ca ..
namaḥ svāhāyai svadhāyai nityameva namonamaḥ .. 114 ..
16.206.d:
देवताभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च महायोगिभ्य एव च ..
नमः स्वाहायै स्वधायै नित्यमेव नमोनमः .. 114 ..
16.206.m: "To the gods, to the ancestors, and to the great yogins; / Homage to svāhā, to svadhā, always homage, homage!"

16.206.s:
ādyāvasāne śrāddhasya trirāvartamimaṃ japan ..
aśvamedhaphalaṃ hyetadvipraiḥ saṃjñāya pūjitam ..115 ..
16.206.d:
आद्यावसाने श्राद्धस्य त्रिरावर्तमिमं जपन् ..
अश्वमेधफलं ह्येतद्विप्रैः संज्ञाय पूजितम् ..115 ..
16.206.m: Reciting this with three repetitions at the beginning and the end of the śrāddha / [yields] the fruit of a horse sacrifice; it is indeed revered having been understood by the brahmins.

16.206.s:
piṇḍanirvapaṇe vāpi japedenaṃ samāhitaḥ ..
pitaraḥ kṣipramāyānti rākṣasāḥ pradravanti ca .. 116 ..
16.206.d:
पिण्डनिर्वपणे वापि जपेदेनं समाहितः ..
पितरः क्षिप्रमायान्ति राक्षसाः प्रद्रवन्ति च .. 116 ..
16.206.m: Or, with a collected mind, one should recite this during the offering of the rice balls. / The ancestors arrive swiftly, and the rākṣasas flee.

16.206.s: saptārciṣaṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvakāmaśubhapradam .. 117 ..
16.206.d: सप्तार्चिषं प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वकामशुभप्रदम् .. 117 ..
16.206.m: I shall proclaim the seven-flamed hymn (saptārcis), granting all desires and good fortune:

16.206.s:
amūrtānāṃ ca mūrtānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ dīptatejasām ..
namasyāmi sadā teṣāṃ dhyāyināṃ divyacakṣuṣām .. 118 ..
16.206.d:
अमूर्तानां च मूर्तानां पितॄणां दीप्ततेजसाम् ..
नमस्यामि सदा तेषां ध्यायिनां दिव्यचक्षुषाम् .. 118 ..
16.206.m: "To the formless and the embodied ancestors of blazing splendour, / To those who meditate, endowed with divine vision, I always bow.

16.206.s:
indrādīnāṃ ca netāro dakṣamārīcayastayā ..
tānnamasyāmi sarvānvai pitṝṃścaivauṣadhīstathā .. 119 ..
16.206.d:
इन्द्रादीनां च नेतारो दक्षमारीचयस्तया ..
तान्नमस्यामि सर्वान्वै पितॄंश्चैवौषधीस्तथा .. 119 ..
16.206.m: The leaders of Indra and the others, Dakṣa, the descendants of Marīci, and so on— / To all of them, the ancestors, and to the plants, I bow.

16.206.s:
nakṣatrāṇāṃ grahāṇāṃ ca vāyvagnyośca pitṝnapi ..
dyāvāpṛthivyośca sadā namasyāmi kṛtāñjaliḥ .. 7.1.206.120 ..
16.206.d:
नक्षत्राणां ग्रहाणां च वाय्वग्न्योश्च पितॄनपि ..
द्यावापृथिव्योश्च सदा नमस्यामि कृताञ्जलिः .. 7.1.206.120 ..
16.206.m: To the ancestors of the lunar mansions and the planets, and of Wind and Fire, / And of Heaven and Earth, I always bow with folded hands.

16.206.s:
namaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ saptabhyo namo lokeṣu saptasu ..
svayaṃbhuve namasyāmo brahmaṇe yogacakṣuṣe ..121..
16.206.d:
नमः पितृभ्यः सप्तभ्यो नमो लोकेषु सप्तसु ..
स्वयंभुवे नमस्यामो ब्रह्मणे योगचक्षुषे ..121..
16.206.m: Homage to the seven ancestors! Homage [to them] in the seven worlds! / We bow to the self-manifest Brahmā, who has the eye of yoga."

16.206.s:
etattvaduktaṃ saptarṣibrahmarṣigaṇasevitam ..
pavitraṃ paramaṃ hyetacchrīmadrakṣovināśanam .. 122..
16.206.d:
एतत्त्वदुक्तं सप्तर्षिब्रह्मर्षिगणसेवितम् ..
पवित्रं परमं ह्येतच्छ्रीमद्रक्षोविनाशनम् .. 122..
16.206.m: This has been declared to you, attended upon by the assembly of the seven seers and brahmin seers; / It is supremely purifying, auspicious, and destroys demons.

16.206.s:
anena vidhinā yuktastrīnvārāṃstu japennaraḥ ..
bhaktyā paramayā yuktaḥ śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ ..123..
16.206.d:
अनेन विधिना युक्तस्त्रीन्वारांस्तु जपेन्नरः ..
भक्त्या परमया युक्तः श्रद्दधानो जितेन्द्रियः ..123..
16.206.m: A man endowed with this rule should recite it three times, / Endowed with supreme devotion, full of faith, and with senses subdued.

16.206.s:
saptārciṣaṃ japedyastu nityameva samāhitaḥ ..
sa tu saptasamudrāyāḥ pṛthivyā ekarāḍbhavet ..124..
16.206.d:
सप्तार्चिषं जपेद्यस्तु नित्यमेव समाहितः ..
स तु सप्तसमुद्रायाः पृथिव्या एकराड्भवेत् ..124..
16.206.m: He who recites the saptārcis constantly with a concentrated mind / Shall become the sole king of the earth consisting of the seven oceans.

16.206.s:
śrāddhakalpaṃ paṭhedyo vai sa bhavetpaṃktipāvanaḥ ..
aṣṭādaśānāṃ vidyānāṃ sa ca vai pāragaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 125 ..
16.206.d:
श्राद्धकल्पं पठेद्यो वै स भवेत्पंक्तिपावनः ..
अष्टादशानां विद्यानां स च वै पारगः स्मृतः .. 125 ..
16.206.m: He who recites the Śrāddhakalpa becomes one who purifies his company; / And he is considered a master of the eighteen disciplines.

16.206.s:
pūjāṃ puṣṭiṃ smṛtiṃ medhāṃ rājyamārogyameva ca ..
prītā nityaṃ prayacchanti mānuṣāṇāṃ pitāmahāḥ .. 126 ..
16.206.d:
पूजां पुष्टिं स्मृतिं मेधां राज्यमारोग्यमेव च ..
प्रीता नित्यं प्रयच्छन्ति मानुषाणां पितामहाः .. 126 ..
16.206.m: Honour, nourishment, memory, intelligence, sovereignty, and freedom from disease— / Pleased, the grandfathers grant these always to human beings.

16.206.s:
evaṃ prabhāsakṣetre sa sarasvatyabdhisaṃgame ..
kuryācchrāddhaṃ vidhānena prabhāse caiva bhāmini .. 127 ..
16.206.d:
एवं प्रभासक्षेत्रे स सरस्वत्यब्धिसंगमे ..
कुर्याच्छ्राद्धं विधानेन प्रभासे चैव भामिनि .. 127 ..
16.206.m: Thus, in the sacred field of Prabhāsa, at the confluence of the Sarasvatī and the ocean, / One should perform the śrāddha according to the injunction, O beautiful woman, in Prabhāsa.

16.206.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsa kṣetramāhātmye sarasvatyabdhisaṃgame śrāddhakalpe śrāddhavidhivarṇanaṃnāma ṣaḍuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 206 ..
16.206.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभास क्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सरस्वत्यब्धिसंगमे श्राद्धकल्पे श्राद्धविधिवर्णनंनाम षडुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 206 ..
16.206.m: Thus ends the two hundred and sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Procedure of Śrāddha' in the Śrāddhakalpa at the confluence of the Sarasvatī and the ocean, in the Māhātmya of the Prabhāsa sacred field, in the first [part of the] Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

16.207.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi śrāddhadānānyanukramāt ..
tāraṇāya ca bhūtānāṃ sarasvatyabdhisaṃgame .. 1 ..
16.207.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि श्राद्धदानान्यनुक्रमात् ..
तारणाय च भूतानां सरस्वत्यब्धिसंगमे .. 1 ..
16.207.m: Īśvara said: / Īśvara said: / Hereafter I shall explain the gifts for the śrāddha in due order, / For the deliverance of living beings at the confluence of the Sarasvatī and the ocean.

16.207.s:
loke śreṣṭhatamaṃ sarvaṃ hyātmanaścāpi yatpriyam ..
sarvaṃ pitṝṇāṃ dātavyaṃ tadevākṣayyamicchatām .. 2 ..
16.207.d:
लोके श्रेष्ठतमं सर्वं ह्यात्मनश्चापि यत्प्रियम् ..
सर्वं पितॄणां दातव्यं तदेवाक्षय्यमिच्छताम् .. 2 ..
16.207.m: Whatever is best in the world, and whatever is dear to oneself, / All that should be given to the ancestors by those desiring imperishable [rewards].

16.207.s:
jāṃbūnadamayaṃ divyaṃ vimānaṃ sūryasannibham ..
divyāpsarobhiḥ saṃkīrṇamannado labhate'kṣayam .. 3 ..
16.207.d:
जांबूनदमयं दिव्यं विमानं सूर्यसन्निभम् ..
दिव्याप्सरोभिः संकीर्णमन्नदो लभतेऽक्षयम् .. 3 ..
16.207.m: A celestial aerial chariot made of gold from the Jambu river, resembling the sun, / Crowded with celestial apsarases, imperishable, the giver of food obtains.

16.207.s:
ācchādanaṃ tu yo dadyādahataṃ śrāddhakarmaṇi ..
āyuḥ prakāśamaiśvaryaṃ rūpaṃ tu labhate ca saḥ .. 4 ..
16.207.d:
आच्छादनं तु यो दद्यादहतं श्राद्धकर्मणि ..
आयुः प्रकाशमैश्वर्यं रूपं तु लभते च सः .. 4 ..
16.207.m: He who gives uncut clothing in the śrāddha rite / Obtains long life, radiance, lordship, and beauty.

16.207.s:
kamaṇḍaluṃ ca yo dadyādbrāhmaṇe vedapārage ..
madhukṣīrasravā dhenurdātāramanugacchati .. 5 ..
16.207.d:
कमण्डलुं च यो दद्याद्ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे ..
मधुक्षीरस्रवा धेनुर्दातारमनुगच्छति .. 5 ..
16.207.m: And he who gives a water pot to a brahmin who has mastered the Veda, / A cow flowing with honey and milk follows that giver.

16.207.s:
yaḥ śrāddhe abhayaṃ dadyātprāṇināṃ jīvitaiṣiṇām ..
aśvadānasahasreṇa rathadānaśatena ca ..
dantināṃ ca sahasreṇa abhayaṃ ca viśiṣyate .. 6 ..
16.207.d:
यः श्राद्धे अभयं दद्यात्प्राणिनां जीवितैषिणाम् ..
अश्वदानसहस्रेण रथदानशतेन च ..
दन्तिनां च सहस्रेण अभयं च विशिष्यते .. 6 ..
16.207.m: He who gives freedom from fear at a śrāddha to living beings desiring life, / [Compared] with the gift of a thousand horses, a hundred chariots, / And a thousand tuskers, the gift of freedom from fear is superior.

16.207.s:
yāni ratnāni medinyāṃ vāhanāni striyastathā ..
kṣipraṃ prāpnoti tatsarvaṃ pitṛbhaktastu mānavaḥ .. 7 ..
16.207.d:
यानि रत्नानि मेदिन्यां वाहनानि स्त्रियस्तथा ..
क्षिप्रं प्राप्नोति तत्सर्वं पितृभक्तस्तु मानवः .. 7 ..
16.207.m: Whatever gems there are on earth, vehicles, and women, / A man devoted to the ancestors swiftly obtains all that.

16.207.s:
pitaraḥ sarvalokeṣu tithikāleṣu devatāḥ ..
sarve puruṣamāyāṃti nipānamiva dhenavaḥ .. 8 ..
16.207.d:
पितरः सर्वलोकेषु तिथिकालेषु देवताः ..
सर्वे पुरुषमायांति निपानमिव धेनवः .. 8 ..
16.207.m: The ancestors, gods in all worlds, at the times of the lunar days, / All approach the man, like cows approaching a water reservoir.

16.207.s:
mā sma te pratigaccheyuḥ parvakāle hyapūjitāḥ ..
moghāsteṣāṃ bhavantvāśāḥ paratreha ca mā kvacit .. 9 ..
16.207.d:
मा स्म ते प्रतिगच्छेयुः पर्वकाले ह्यपूजिताः ..
मोघास्तेषां भवन्त्वाशाः परत्रेह च मा क्वचित् .. 9 ..
16.207.m: Let them not return unhonoured at the time of the festival! / May their hopes never be in vain, here or in the hereafter.

16.207.s:
sarasvatyāstu sānnidhyaṃ yastvekaṃ bhojayeddvijam ..
koṭibhojyaphalaṃ tasya jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 7.1.207.10 ..
16.207.d:
सरस्वत्यास्तु सान्निध्यं यस्त्वेकं भोजयेद्द्विजम् ..
कोटिभोज्यफलं तस्य जायते नात्र संशयः .. 7.1.207.10 ..
16.207.m: He who feeds just one twice-born in the presence of the Sarasvatī, / Gains the fruit of feeding ten million; of this there is no doubt.

16.207.s:
amāvāsyāṃ naro yastu parānnamupabhuñjate ..
tasya māsakṛtaṃ puṇyamannadātuḥ prajāyate .. 11 ..
16.207.d:
अमावास्यां नरो यस्तु परान्नमुपभुञ्जते ..
तस्य मासकृतं पुण्यमन्नदातुः प्रजायते .. 11 ..
16.207.m: The man who eats the food of another on the new moon day— / His merit acquired during the month accrues to the giver of the food.

16.207.s:
ṣaṇmāsamayane bhuṃkte trīnmāsānviṣuve smṛtam ..
varṣairdvādaśabhiścaiva yatpuṇyaṃ samupārjitam ..
tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti bhuktvā sūryendusaṃplave .. 12 ..
16.207.d:
षण्मासमयने भुंक्ते त्रीन्मासान्विषुवे स्मृतम् ..
वर्षैर्द्वादशभिश्चैव यत्पुण्यं समुपार्जितम् ..
तत्सर्वं विलयं याति भुक्त्वा सूर्येन्दुसंप्लवे .. 12 ..
16.207.m: If he eats [another's food] at the solstice, [it consumes the merit of] six months; at the equinox, it is taught to be three months. / Whatever merit was acquired over twelve years, / All that is lost by eating during a solar or lunar eclipse.

16.207.s:
sāgraṃ māsaṃ raveḥ krāntāvādyaśrāddhe trivatsaram ..
māsike'pyatha varṣasya ṣaṇmāse tvardhavatsaram .. 13 ..
16.207.d:
साग्रं मासं रवेः क्रान्तावाद्यश्राद्धे त्रिवत्सरम् ..
मासिकेऽप्यथ वर्षस्य षण्मासे त्वर्धवत्सरम् .. 13 ..
16.207.m: A full month at the transit of the sun; at the initial śrāddha, three years; / At the monthly rite, a year; at the six-monthly, half a year;

16.207.s:
tathā saṃcayanaśrāddhe jātijanmakṛtaṃ nṛṇām ..
mṛta śayyāpratigrāhī vedasyaiva ca vikrayī ..
brahmasvahārī ca narastasya śuddhirna vidyate. .. 14 ..
16.207.d:
तथा संचयनश्राद्धे जातिजन्मकृतं नृणाम् ..
मृत शय्याप्रतिग्राही वेदस्यैव च विक्रयी ..
ब्रह्मस्वहारी च नरस्तस्य शुद्धिर्न विद्यते. .. 14 ..
16.207.m: Likewise, at the collection śrāddha, [the merit] acquired throughout one's birth and existence is destroyed. / One who accepts the bed of a dead man, one who sells the Veda, / And a man who steals the property of brahmins: for him there is no purification.

16.207.s:
taḍāgānāṃ sahasreṇa hyaśvamedhaśatena ca ..
gavāṃ koṭi pradānena bhūmihartā na śuddhyati .. 15 ..
16.207.d:
तडागानां सहस्रेण ह्यश्वमेधशतेन च ..
गवां कोटि प्रदानेन भूमिहर्ता न शुद्ध्यति .. 15 ..
16.207.m: Not by a thousand tanks, nor by a hundred horse sacrifices, / Nor by the gift of ten million cows does a stealer of land become purified.

16.207.s:
suvarṇamāṣaṃ gāmekāṃ bhūmerapyardhamaṃgulam ..
harannarakamāpnoti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam .. 16 ..
16.207.d:
सुवर्णमाषं गामेकां भूमेरप्यर्धमंगुलम् ..
हरन्नरकमाप्नोति यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् .. 16 ..
16.207.m: Stealing even a māṣa of gold, a single cow, or half an inch of land, / a man attains hell until the dissolution of all beings. // 16

16.207.s:
brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ daridrasya tu yaddhanam ..
guroḥ patnī hiraṇyaṃ ca svargasthamapi pātayet. .. 17 ..
16.207.d:
ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं दरिद्रस्य तु यद्धनम् ..
गुरोः पत्नी हिरण्यं च स्वर्गस्थमपि पातयेत्. .. 17 ..
16.207.m: Killing a brahmin, drinking liquor, [stealing] the wealth of a poor person, / [violating] the guru's wife, and [stealing] gold—[any of these] causes even one in heaven to fall. // 17

16.207.s:
sahasrasaṃmitā dhenuranaḍvāndaśa dhenavaḥ ..
daśānaḍutsamaṃ yānaṃ daśayānasamo hayaḥ .. 18 ..
16.207.d:
सहस्रसंमिता धेनुरनड्वान्दश धेनवः ..
दशानडुत्समं यानं दशयानसमो हयः .. 18 ..
16.207.m: A cow is worth a thousand [gifts]; an ox is worth ten cows; / a vehicle is equal to ten oxen; a horse is equal to ten vehicles; // 18

16.207.s:
daśahayasamā kanyā bhūmidānaṃ tato'dhikam ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena vikrayaṃ naiva kārayet .. 19 ..
16.207.d:
दशहयसमा कन्या भूमिदानं ततोऽधिकम् ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन विक्रयं नैव कारयेत् .. 19 ..
16.207.m: a maiden is equal to ten horses; the gift of land is greater than that. / Therefore, by every effort, one must never allow [land] to be sold. // 19

16.207.s:
viśeṣato mahākṣetre sarvapātakanāśane ..
citikāṣṭhaṃ ca vai spṛṣṭvā yajñayūpāṃstathaiva ca ..
vedavikrayakartāraṃ spṛṣṭvā snānaṃ vidhīyate .. 7.1.207.20 ..
16.207.d:
विशेषतो महाक्षेत्रे सर्वपातकनाशने ..
चितिकाष्ठं च वै स्पृष्ट्वा यज्ञयूपांस्तथैव च ..
वेदविक्रयकर्तारं स्पृष्ट्वा स्नानं विधीयते .. 7.1.207.20 ..
16.207.m: Especially in a great sacred field that destroys all sins: / having touched wood from a funeral pyre, or sacrificial posts, / or having touched someone who sells the Veda, a ritual ablution is prescribed. // 7.1.207.20

16.207.s:
ādeśaṃ paṭhate yastu ādeśaṃ ca dadāti yaḥ ..
dvāvetau pāpakarmāṇau pātālatalavāsinau .. 21 ..
16.207.d:
आदेशं पठते यस्तु आदेशं च ददाति यः ..
द्वावेतौ पापकर्माणौ पातालतलवासिनौ .. 21 ..
16.207.m: Whoever recites a royal edict [for gain] and whoever gives an edict— / both of these evil-doers are destined to dwell in the depths of Pātāla. // 21

16.207.s:
ādeśaṃ paṭhate yastu rājadvāre tu mānavaḥ ..
so'pi devi bhavedvṛkṣa ūṣare kaṃṭakāvṛtaḥ ..
sthito vai nṛpatidvāri yaḥ kuryādvedavikrayam ..22..
16.207.d:
आदेशं पठते यस्तु राजद्वारे तु मानवः ..
सोऽपि देवि भवेद्वृक्ष ऊषरे कंटकावृतः ..
स्थितो वै नृपतिद्वारि यः कुर्याद्वेदविक्रयम् ..22..
16.207.m: The man who recites a royal edict at the king’s gate, / he too, O goddess, becomes a thorn-covered tree in a barren desert— / [and likewise] one who stays at the king’s gate and sells the Veda. // 22

16.207.s:
brahmahatyāsamaṃ pāpaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati ..
varaṃ kurvandhruvaṃ devi na kuryādvedavikrayam ..23..
16.207.d:
ब्रह्महत्यासमं पापं न भूतं न भविष्यति ..
वरं कुर्वन्ध्रुवं देवि न कुर्याद्वेदविक्रयम् ..23..
16.207.m: A sin equal to killing a brahmin has never existed nor ever will. / It would be better to commit [other wrongs], O goddess, but one must certainly never sell the Veda. // 23

16.207.s:
hatvā gāśca varaṃ māṃsaṃ bhakṣayīta dvijādhamaḥ ..
varaṃ jīvetsamaṃ mlecchairna kuryādvedavikrayam .. 24 ..
16.207.d:
हत्वा गाश्च वरं मांसं भक्षयीत द्विजाधमः ..
वरं जीवेत्समं म्लेच्छैर्न कुर्याद्वेदविक्रयम् .. 24 ..
16.207.m: It would be better for the lowest of the twice-born to slaughter cows and eat their meat; / it would be better to live among the barbarians, rather than sell the Veda. // 24

16.207.s:
pratyakṣoktiḥ pratyayaśca praśnapūrvaḥ pratigrahaḥ ..
yājanā'dhyāpane vādaḥ ṣaḍvidho vedavikrayaḥ .. 25 ..
16.207.d:
प्रत्यक्षोक्तिः प्रत्ययश्च प्रश्नपूर्वः प्रतिग्रहः ..
याजनाऽध्यापने वादः षड्विधो वेदविक्रयः .. 25 ..
16.207.m: A direct demand, an assurance, acceptance following inquiry, / bargaining over officiating or over teaching—selling the Veda is of six kinds. // 25

16.207.s:
vedākṣarāṇi yāvanti niyuṃkte svārthakāraṇāt ..
tāvatīrbhrūṇahatyā vai prāpnuyādvedavikrayī .. 26 ..
16.207.d:
वेदाक्षराणि यावन्ति नियुंक्ते स्वार्थकारणात् ..
तावतीर्भ्रूणहत्या वै प्राप्नुयाद्वेदविक्रयी .. 26 ..
16.207.m: For as many syllables of the Veda as he employs for selfish purposes, / indeed, so many murders of an embryo does the seller of the Veda incur. // 26

16.207.s:
vedānuyogādyo dadyādbrāhmaṇāya pratigraham ..
sa pūrvaṃ narakaṃ yāti brāhmaṇastadanantaram .. 27 ..
16.207.d:
वेदानुयोगाद्यो दद्याद्ब्राह्मणाय प्रतिग्रहम् ..
स पूर्वं नरकं याति ब्राह्मणस्तदनन्तरम् .. 27 ..
16.207.m: Whoever gives an offering to a brahmin on account of [his] recitation of the Veda, / he goes to hell first, and the brahmin immediately after. // 27

16.207.s:
vaiśvadevena hīnā ye hīnāścātithyato'pi ye ..
karmaṇā sarvavṛṣalā vedayuktā hyapi dvijāḥ .. 28 ..
16.207.d:
वैश्वदेवेन हीना ये हीनाश्चातिथ्यतोऽपि ये ..
कर्मणा सर्ववृषला वेदयुक्ता ह्यपि द्विजाः .. 28 ..
16.207.m: Those who are destitute of the vaiśvadeva rite and those who lack hospitality to guests, / are by their conduct entirely Śūdras, even if they are twice-born endowed with the Veda. // 28

16.207.s:
yeṣāmadhyayanaṃ nāsti ye ca kecidanagnayaḥ ..
kulaṃ vā'śrotriyaṃ yeṣāṃ te sarve śūdrajātayaḥ .. 29 ..
16.207.d:
येषामध्ययनं नास्ति ये च केचिदनग्नयः ..
कुलं वाऽश्रोत्रियं येषां ते सर्वे शूद्रजातयः .. 29 ..
16.207.m: Those who do not study, those who keep no sacred fire, / or those whose family is unlearned in the Veda—they all have the status of Śūdras. // 29

16.207.s:
mṛte'hani pituryastu na kuryācchrāddhamādarāt ..
mātuścaiva varārohe sa dvijaḥ śūdrasaṃnibhaḥ .. 7.1.207.30 ..
16.207.d:
मृतेऽहनि पितुर्यस्तु न कुर्याच्छ्राद्धमादरात् ..
मातुश्चैव वरारोहे स द्विजः शूद्रसंनिभः .. 7.1.207.30 ..
16.207.m: He who does not perform with devotion the śrāddha on the anniversary of the father's death, / or of the mother's, O fair-hipped goddess, that twice-born is equal to a Śūdra. // 7.1.207.30

16.207.s:
mṛtake yastu bhuñjīta gṛhītaśaśibhāskare ..
gajacchāyāsu yaḥ kaścittaṃ ca śūdravadācaret .. 31 ..
16.207.d:
मृतके यस्तु भुञ्जीत गृहीतशशिभास्करे ..
गजच्छायासु यः कश्चित्तं च शूद्रवदाचरेत् .. 31 ..
16.207.m: He who eats during a period of death-impurity, or during an eclipse of the moon or sun, / or at an elephant's shadow—one should treat him as a Śūdra. // 31

16.207.s:
brahmacāriṇi yajñe ca yatau śilpini dīkṣite ..
yajñe vivāhe satre ca sūtakaṃ na kadācana .. 32 ..
16.207.d:
ब्रह्मचारिणि यज्ञे च यतौ शिल्पिनि दीक्षिते ..
यज्ञे विवाहे सत्रे च सूतकं न कदाचन .. 32 ..
16.207.m: For a celibate student, at a sacrifice, for an ascetic, for an artisan, for an initiated person, / at a sacrificial rite, at a marriage, and at a long sacrificial session, there is never ritual impurity. // 32

16.207.s:
gorakṣakānvaṇijakāṃstathā kārukuśīlavān ..
spṛśyānvārdhuṣikāṃścaiva viprānśūdravadācaret .. 33 ..
16.207.d:
गोरक्षकान्वणिजकांस्तथा कारुकुशीलवान् ..
स्पृश्यान्वार्धुषिकांश्चैव विप्रान्शूद्रवदाचरेत् .. 33 ..
16.207.m: Cowherds, traders, artisans, bards, / and usurers—even if they are brahmins, one should treat them as Śūdras. // 33

16.207.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ patanīyeṣu vartamāno vikarmasu ..
dāmbhiko duṣkṛtaprāyaḥ sa ca śūdrasamaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 34 ..
16.207.d:
ब्राह्मणः पतनीयेषु वर्तमानो विकर्मसु ..
दाम्भिको दुष्कृतप्रायः स च शूद्रसमः स्मृतः .. 34 ..
16.207.m: A brahmin who engages in degrading misdeeds, / hypocritical and full of evil deeds, is considered equal to a Śūdra. // 34

16.207.s:
asnātāśī malaṃ bhuṃkte ajāpī pūyaśoṇitam ..
ahutvā tu kṛmīnbhuṃkte adattvā viṣabhojanam .. 35 ..
16.207.d:
अस्नाताशी मलं भुंक्ते अजापी पूयशोणितम् ..
अहुत्वा तु कृमीन्भुंक्ते अदत्त्वा विषभोजनम् .. 35 ..
16.207.m: One who eats without having bathed eats filth; one who recites no prayers [eats] pus and blood; / one who eats without offering into the fire eats worms; one who eats without giving [to others] eats poison. // 35

16.207.s:
parānnena tu bhuktena mithunaṃ yo'dhigacchati ..
yasyānnaṃ tasya te putrā annācchukraṃ pravartate .. 36 ..
16.207.d:
परान्नेन तु भुक्तेन मिथुनं योऽधिगच्छति ..
यस्यान्नं तस्य ते पुत्रा अन्नाच्छुक्रं प्रवर्तते .. 36 ..
16.207.m: If someone unites with a woman after eating another's food, / the sons belong to him whose food it was, for semen arises from food. // 36

16.207.s:
rājānnaṃ teja ādatte śūdrānnaṃ brahmavarcasam ..
āyuḥ suvarṇakārānnaṃ yaśaścarmāvakartinaḥ .. 37 ..
16.207.d:
राजान्नं तेज आदत्ते शूद्रान्नं ब्रह्मवर्चसम् ..
आयुः सुवर्णकारान्नं यशश्चर्मावकर्तिनः .. 37 ..
16.207.m: The food of a king takes away brilliance; the food of a Śūdra takes away spiritual radiance; / the food of a goldsmith takes away lifespan; that of a leather-cutter takes away fame. // 37

16.207.s:
kārukānnaṃ prajā hanti balaṃ nirṇejakasya ca ..
gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca lokebhyaḥ parikṛntati .. 38 ..
16.207.d:
कारुकान्नं प्रजा हन्ति बलं निर्णेजकस्य च ..
गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च लोकेभ्यः परिकृन्तति .. 38 ..
16.207.m: The food of an artisan destroys offspring; that of a washerman destroys strength; / the food of a guild and the food of a courtesan cut one off from the heavenly worlds. // 38

16.207.s:
pūyaṃ cikitsakasyānnaṃ puṃścalyāstvannamindriyam ..
viṣṭhā vārdhuṣikasyānnaṃ śastravikrayiṇo malam .. 39 ..
16.207.d:
पूयं चिकित्सकस्यान्नं पुंश्चल्यास्त्वन्नमिन्द्रियम् ..
विष्ठा वार्धुषिकस्यान्नं शस्त्रविक्रयिणो मलम् .. 39 ..
16.207.m: The food of a physician is pus; the food of an unchaste woman is sexual fluid; / the food of a usurer is excrement; that of an arm-seller is dirt. // 39

16.207.s:
gāyatrīsāramātro'pi varaṃ vipraḥ suyantritaḥ ..
nāyaṃtritaścaturvedī sarvāśī sarvavikrayī .. 7.1.207.40 ..
16.207.d:
गायत्रीसारमात्रोऽपि वरं विप्रः सुयन्त्रितः ..
नायंत्रितश्चतुर्वेदी सर्वाशी सर्वविक्रयी .. 7.1.207.40 ..
16.207.m: Better is a well-controlled brahmin whose only knowledge is the essence of the Gāyatrī, / than an uncontrolled knower of the four Vedas who eats everything and sells everything. // 7.1.207.40

16.207.s:
sadyaḥ patati māṃsena lākṣayā lavaṇena ca ..
tryaheṇa śūdro bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ kṣīravikrayāt .. 41 ..
16.207.d:
सद्यः पतति मांसेन लाक्षया लवणेन च ..
त्र्यहेण शूद्रो भवति ब्राह्मणः क्षीरविक्रयात् .. 41 ..
16.207.m: [A brahmin] falls instantly through [selling] meat, lac, and salt; / through selling milk, a brahmin becomes a Śūdra in three days. // 41

16.207.s:
rasā rasairniyaṃtavyā na tveva lavaṇaṃ rasaiḥ ..
kṛtānnaṃ ca kṛtānnena tilā dhānyena tatsamāḥ .. 42 ..
16.207.d:
रसा रसैर्नियंतव्या न त्वेव लवणं रसैः ..
कृतान्नं च कृतान्नेन तिला धान्येन तत्समाः .. 42 ..
16.207.m: Liquids may be exchanged for liquids, but never salt for liquids; / cooked food [may be exchanged] for cooked food, and sesame seeds for their equal in grain. // 42

16.207.s:
bhojanābhyañjanāddānādyadanyatkurute tilaiḥ ..
kṛmibhūtaḥ sa viṣṭhāyāṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha majjati .. 43 ..
16.207.d:
भोजनाभ्यञ्जनाद्दानाद्यदन्यत्कुरुते तिलैः ..
कृमिभूतः स विष्ठायां पितृभिः सह मज्जति .. 43 ..
16.207.m: Whatever else one does with sesame seeds other than eating, anointing, or giving them away, / he sinks into excrement along with his ancestors, turning into a worm. // 43

16.207.s:
apūpaśca hiraṇyaṃ ca gāmaśvaṃ pṛthivīṃ tilān ..
avidvānpratigṛhṇāti bhasmībhavati kāṣṭhavat ..44..
16.207.d:
अपूपश्च हिरण्यं च गामश्वं पृथिवीं तिलान् ..
अविद्वान्प्रतिगृह्णाति भस्मीभवति काष्ठवत् ..44..
16.207.m: If an ignorant man accepts cakes, gold, / a cow, a horse, land, or sesame seeds, he turns to ashes like wood. // 44

16.207.s:
hiraṇyamāyu ratnaṃ ca bhūrgauścākarṣatastanum ..
aśvaścakṣustvacaṃ vāso ghṛtaṃ tejastilāḥ prajāḥ .. 45 .. tila
16.207.d:
हिरण्यमायु रत्नं च भूर्गौश्चाकर्षतस्तनुम् ..
अश्वश्चक्षुस्त्वचं वासो घृतं तेजस्तिलाः प्रजाः .. 45 .. तिल
16.207.m: Gold and jewels [destroy] longevity; land and a cow drain the physical body; / a horse takes away sight; cloth takes away the skin; ghee takes away brilliance; sesame seeds take away offspring. // 45

16.207.s:
agnihotrī tapasvī ca kṣaṇavānkriyate yadi ..
agnihotraṃ tapaścaiva sarvaṃ taddhanino dhanam .. 46 ..
16.207.d:
अग्निहोत्री तपस्वी च क्षणवान्क्रियते यदि ..
अग्निहोत्रं तपश्चैव सर्वं तद्धनिनो धनम् .. 46 ..
16.207.m: If a keeper of the sacred fire and an ascetic is hired for an occasion, / all his fire offerings and austerity become the property of the rich employer. // 46

16.207.s:
somavikrayaṇe viṣṭhā bheṣaje pūyaśoṇitam ..
naṣṭaṃ devalake dānaṃ hyapratiṣṭhaṃ ca vārdhuke .. 47 ..
16.207.d:
सोमविक्रयणे विष्ठा भेषजे पूयशोणितम् ..
नष्टं देवलके दानं ह्यप्रतिष्ठं च वार्धुके .. 47 ..
16.207.m: In the selling of soma is excrement; in medicine, pus and blood; / a gift given to a temple priest is wasted, and [a gift given] to a usurer brings no foundation. // 47

16.207.s:
devārcanaparo vipro vittārthī bhuvanatraye ..
asau devalakonāma havyakavyeṣu garhitaḥ .. 48 ..
16.207.d:
देवार्चनपरो विप्रो वित्तार्थी भुवनत्रये ..
असौ देवलकोनाम हव्यकव्येषु गर्हितः .. 48 ..
16.207.m: A brahmin devoted to the worship of gods for the sake of wealth in the three worlds / is called a devalaka; he is condemned in rites for gods and ancestors. // 48

16.207.s:
bhrāturmṛtasyabhāyāyāṃ yo gacchetkāmapūrvakam ..
dharmeṇāpi niyuktāyāṃ sa jñeyo didhiṣūpatiḥ .. 49 ..
16.207.d:
भ्रातुर्मृतस्यभायायां यो गच्छेत्कामपूर्वकम् ..
धर्मेणापि नियुक्तायां स ज्ञेयो दिधिषूपतिः .. 49 ..
16.207.m: He who approaches the wife of his deceased brother out of lust, / even if appointed according to law, is known as a didhiṣūpati. // 49

16.207.s:
dārāgnihotrasaṃyogaṃ kurute yo'graje sthite ..
parivettā sa vijñeyaḥ parivittistu pūrvajaḥ .. 7.1.207.50 ..
16.207.d:
दाराग्निहोत्रसंयोगं कुरुते योऽग्रजे स्थिते ..
परिवेत्ता स विज्ञेयः परिवित्तिस्तु पूर्वजः .. 7.1.207.50 ..
16.207.m: He who takes a wife and establishes the sacred fires while his elder brother remains [unmarried] / should be known as a parivettā, and the elder brother as a parivitti. // 7.1.207.50

16.207.s:
yo naro'nyasya vāsāṃsi kūpodyānagṛhāṇi ca ..
adattānyupayuṃjānaḥ sa tatpāpaturīyabhāk .. 51 ..
16.207.d:
यो नरोऽन्यस्य वासांसि कूपोद्यानगृहाणि च ..
अदत्तान्युपयुंजानः स तत्पापतुरीयभाक् .. 51 ..
16.207.m: A man who uses the clothes, wells, gardens, and houses / of another without permission partakes of a fourth of his sins. // 51

16.207.s:
āmantritastu yaḥ śrāddhe vṛṣalyā saha modate ..
dāturyadduṣkṛtaṃ kiñcittatsarvaṃ pratipadyate .. 52 ..
16.207.d:
आमन्त्रितस्तु यः श्राद्धे वृषल्या सह मोदते ..
दातुर्यद्दुष्कृतं किञ्चित्तत्सर्वं प्रतिपद्यते .. 52 ..
16.207.m: One who, having been invited to a śrāddha, enjoys himself with a Śūdra woman, / incurs all whatever evil deed belongs to the donor. // 52

16.207.s:
ṛtāmṛtābhyāṃ jīveta mṛtena pramṛtena vā ..
satyānṛtābhyāṃ jīveta na śvavṛttyā kathaṃcana .. 53 ..
16.207.d:
ऋतामृताभ्यां जीवेत मृतेन प्रमृतेन वा ..
सत्यानृताभ्यां जीवेत न श्ववृत्त्या कथंचन .. 53 ..
16.207.m: One may live by ṛta and amṛta, or by mṛta and pramṛta, / or one may live by satyānṛta, but by a dog's livelihood under no circumstance. // 53

16.207.s:
bhakṣyaṃ nityamṛtaṃ jñeyamamṛtaṃ syādayācitam ..
mṛtaṃ tu vṛddhyājīvitvaṃ pramṛtaṃ karṣaṇaṃ smṛtam .. 54 ..
16.207.d:
भक्ष्यं नित्यमृतं ज्ञेयममृतं स्यादयाचितम् ..
मृतं तु वृद्ध्याजीवित्वं प्रमृतं कर्षणं स्मृतम् .. 54 ..
16.207.m: Gleaned grain is to be known as ṛta; what is unasked for is amṛta; / living by usury is mṛta; agriculture is remembered as pramṛta. // 54

16.207.s:
satyānṛtaṃ ca vāṇijyaṃ tena caivopajīvyate ..
sevā śvavṛttirākhyātā tasmāttāṃ parivarjayeta .. 55 ..
16.207.d:
सत्यानृतं च वाणिज्यं तेन चैवोपजीव्यते ..
सेवा श्ववृत्तिराख्याता तस्मात्तां परिवर्जयेत .. 55 ..
16.207.m: Trade is satyānṛta, and one may sustain oneself by that too; / servitude is called a dog's livelihood, therefore one should avoid it. // 55

16.207.s:
viprayoniṃ samāsādya saṃkaraṃ parivarjayet ..
mānuṣyaṃ durlabhaṃ loke brāhmaṇyamadhikaṃ tataḥ .. 56 ..
16.207.d:
विप्रयोनिं समासाद्य संकरं परिवर्जयेत् ..
मानुष्यं दुर्लभं लोके ब्राह्मण्यमधिकं ततः .. 56 ..
16.207.m: Having attained birth as a brahmin, one should avoid mixture; / human birth is difficult to obtain in the world, and brahminhood even more so. // 56

16.207.s:
ekaśayyāsanaṃ paktirbhāṇḍapakvānnamiśraṇam ..
yājanādhyāpanaṃ yonistathā ca saha bhojanam ..
navadhā saṃkaraḥ prokto na kartavyo'dhamaiḥ saha .. 57 ..
16.207.d:
एकशय्यासनं पक्तिर्भाण्डपक्वान्नमिश्रणम् ..
याजनाध्यापनं योनिस्तथा च सह भोजनम् ..
नवधा संकरः प्रोक्तो न कर्तव्योऽधमैः सह .. 57 ..
16.207.m: Sharing a bed or seat, eating in a common line, mixing pots and cooked food, / officiating at sacrifices, teaching, intermarriage, and dining together— / this mixture is declared to be of nine kinds; it must not be done with degraded persons. // 57

16.207.s:
ajīvankarmaṇā svena vipraḥ kṣāttraṃ samāśrayet ..
vaiśyakarmā'thavā kuryādvārṣalaṃ parivarjayet .. 58 ..
16.207.d:
अजीवन्कर्मणा स्वेन विप्रः क्षात्त्रं समाश्रयेत् ..
वैश्यकर्माऽथवा कुर्याद्वार्षलं परिवर्जयेत् .. 58 ..
16.207.m: If unable to make a living by his own occupation, a brahmin may take up that of a kṣatriya, / or he may perform the work of a vaiśya; but he must avoid that of a Śūdra. // 58

16.207.s:
kusīdaṃ kṛṣivāṇijyaṃ prakurvīta svayaṃ kṛtam ..
āpatkāle svayaṃ kurvansnānena spṛśyate dvijaḥ .. ..59..
16.207.d:
कुसीदं कृषिवाणिज्यं प्रकुर्वीत स्वयं कृतम् ..
आपत्काले स्वयं कुर्वन्स्नानेन स्पृश्यते द्विजः .. ..59..
16.207.m: He may himself engage in moneylending, agriculture, and commerce. / Engaging in them himself in times of distress, the twice-born is purified by ritual ablution. // 59

16.207.s:
labdhalābhaḥ pitṝndevānbrāṃhmaṇāṃścaiva tarpayet ..
te tṛptāstasya tatpāpaṃ śamayaṃti na saṃśayaḥ ..7.1.207.60..
16.207.d:
लब्धलाभः पितॄन्देवान्ब्रांह्मणांश्चैव तर्पयेत् ..
ते तृप्तास्तस्य तत्पापं शमयंति न संशयः ..7.1.207.60..
16.207.m: Having obtained profit, he should satisfy the ancestors, the gods, and brahmins; / they, being satisfied, dispel that sin of his; there is no doubt. // 60

16.207.s:
jalagośakaṭārāmayāñcāvṛddhivaṇikkriyāḥ ..
anūpaṃ parvato rājā durbhikṣe jīvikā smṛtāḥ .. 61 ..
16.207.d:
जलगोशकटारामयाञ्चावृद्धिवणिक्क्रियाः ..
अनूपं पर्वतो राजा दुर्भिक्षे जीविका स्मृताः .. 61 ..
16.207.m: Water, cattle, carts, orchards, begging, usury, and trade activities, / marshland, mountains, and the king are declared to be means of livelihood during a famine. // 61

16.207.s:
asato'pi samādāya sādhubhyo yaḥ prayacchati ..
dhanaṃ svāminamātmānaṃ saṃtārayati dustarāt .. 62 ..
16.207.d:
असतोऽपि समादाय साधुभ्यो यः प्रयच्छति ..
धनं स्वामिनमात्मानं संतारयति दुस्तरात् .. 62 ..
16.207.m: Whoever takes wealth even from an unworthy person and gives it to the virtuous, / delivers its owner and himself from what is difficult to cross. // 62

16.207.s:
śūdre samaguṇaṃ dānaṃ vaiśye taddviguṇaṃ smṛtam ..
śrotriye tacca sāhasramanantaṃ cāgnihotrike .. 63 ..
16.207.d:
शूद्रे समगुणं दानं वैश्ये तद्द्विगुणं स्मृतम् ..
श्रोत्रिये तच्च साहस्रमनन्तं चाग्निहोत्रिके .. 63 ..
16.207.m: A gift to a Śūdra brings equal merit; to a Vaiśya, it is taught to be twofold; / to a scholar of the Veda, it is a thousandfold; and to an Agnihotrin, it is infinite. // 63

16.207.s:
brāhmaṇātikramo nāsti nācaredyo vyavasthitim ..
jvalaṃtamagnimutsṛjya na hi bhasmani hūyate .. 64 ..
16.207.d:
ब्राह्मणातिक्रमो नास्ति नाचरेद्यो व्यवस्थितिम् ..
ज्वलंतमग्निमुत्सृज्य न हि भस्मनि हूयते .. 64 ..
16.207.m: There is no bypassing a brahmin; one should not violate proper order: / bypassing a blazing fire, one does not indeed offer an oblation into ashes. // 64

16.207.s:
vidyātapobhyāṃ hīnena naiva grāhyaḥ pratigrahaḥ ..
gṛhṇanpradātāramadho nayatyātmānameva ca .. 65 ..
16.207.d:
विद्यातपोभ्यां हीनेन नैव ग्राह्यः प्रतिग्रहः ..
गृह्णन्प्रदातारमधो नयत्यात्मानमेव च .. 65 ..
16.207.m: A gift should never be accepted by one devoid of learning and austerity; / accepting it, he drags both the giver and himself downward. // 65

16.207.s:
tasmācchrotriya evārho guṇavāñchīlavāñchuciḥ ..
avyaṃgastatra nirdoṣaḥ pātrāṇāṃ paramaṃ smṛtam .. 66 ..
16.207.d:
तस्माच्छ्रोत्रिय एवार्हो गुणवाञ्छीलवाञ्छुचिः ..
अव्यंगस्तत्र निर्दोषः पात्राणां परमं स्मृतम् .. 66 ..
16.207.m: Therefore, only a scholar of the Veda is worthy—virtuous, of good character, pure, / free of bodily defect, and faultless; this is taught to be the highest among recipients. // 66

16.207.s:
kapālasthaṃ yathā toyaṃ śvadṛtau ca yathā payaḥ ..
dūṣitaṃ sthānadoṣeṇa vṛttahīne tathā śrutam .. 67 ..
16.207.d:
कपालस्थं यथा तोयं श्वदृतौ च यथा पयः ..
दूषितं स्थानदोषेण वृत्तहीने तथा श्रुतम् .. 67 ..
16.207.m: Just as water kept in a skull or milk in a dog's skin / is contaminated by the fault of the vessel, so is Vedic knowledge in one lacking right conduct. // 67

16.207.s:
dattaṃ pātramatikramya yadapātre pratigrahaḥ ..
taddattaṃ gāmatikramya gardabhasya gavāhnikam .. 68 ..
16.207.d:
दत्तं पात्रमतिक्रम्य यदपात्रे प्रतिग्रहः ..
तद्दत्तं गामतिक्रम्य गर्दभस्य गवाह्निकम् .. 68 ..
16.207.m: When a gift is accepted by an unworthy recipient, bypassing a worthy recipient, / that gift is like giving daily fodder to a donkey, bypassing a cow. // 68

16.207.s:
vṛttaṃ tasmāttu saṃrakṣedvittameti gataṃ punaḥ ..
akṣīṇo vittataḥ kṣīṇo vṛttatastu hato hataḥ .. 69 ..
16.207.d:
वृत्तं तस्मात्तु संरक्षेद्वित्तमेति गतं पुनः ..
अक्षीणो वित्ततः क्षीणो वृत्ततस्तु हतो हतः .. 69 ..
16.207.m: Therefore, one should preserve conduct; wealth comes and goes again. / One depleted of wealth is not truly ruined, but one ruined in conduct is utterly destroyed. // 69

16.207.s:
prathamaṃ tu gurau dānaṃ dattvā śreṣṭhamanukramāt ..
tato'nyeṣāṃ tu viprāṇāṃ dadyātpātrānurūpataḥ .. 7.1.207.70 ..
16.207.d:
प्रथमं तु गुरौ दानं दत्त्वा श्रेष्ठमनुक्रमात् ..
ततोऽन्येषां तु विप्राणां दद्यात्पात्रानुरूपतः .. 7.1.207.70 ..
16.207.m: First giving the highest gift to the guru in due order, / he should then give to other brahmins according to their worthiness as recipients. // 70

16.207.s:
gurau ca dattaṃ yaddānaṃ dattaṃ pātreṣu mānavaiḥ ..
niṣphalaṃ tadbhavetpretya yātyutādhogatiṃ prati .. 71 ..
16.207.d:
गुरौ च दत्तं यद्दानं दत्तं पात्रेषु मानवैः ..
निष्फलं तद्भवेत्प्रेत्य यात्युताधोगतिं प्रति .. 71 ..
16.207.m: When men have given to other recipients a gift that was [meant to be] given to the guru, / that [gift] becomes fruitless after death, or rather leads to a downward state. // 71

16.207.s:
avamānaṃ guroḥ kṛtvā kopayitvā tu durmatiḥ ..
gurvamānahato mūḍho na śāṃtimadhi gacchati .. 72 ..
16.207.d:
अवमानं गुरोः कृत्वा कोपयित्वा तु दुर्मतिः ..
गुर्वमानहतो मूढो न शांतिमधि गच्छति .. 72 ..
16.207.m: A fool who dishonors his guru and angers him, / struck down by disrespect to his guru, does not attain peace. // 72

16.207.s:
gurorabhāve tatputraṃ tadbhāryāṃ tatsutaṃ vinā ..
putraṃ prapautraṃ dauhitraṃ hyanyaṃ vā tatkulodbhavam .. 73 ..
16.207.d:
गुरोरभावे तत्पुत्रं तद्भार्यां तत्सुतं विना ..
पुत्रं प्रपौत्रं दौहित्रं ह्यन्यं वा तत्कुलोद्भवम् .. 73 ..
16.207.m: In the absence of the guru, [one should give to] his son; failing his son, to his wife; / or to his grandson, great-grandson, daughter's son, or another born in his family. // 73

16.207.s:
paṃcayojanamadhye tu śrūyate svagururyadā ..
tadā nātikrameddānaṃ dadyātpātreṣu mānavaḥ .. 74 ..
16.207.d:
पंचयोजनमध्ये तु श्रूयते स्वगुरुर्यदा ..
तदा नातिक्रमेद्दानं दद्यात्पात्रेषु मानवः .. 74 ..
16.207.m: When one's own guru is heard to be within five yojanas, / then a person should not pass him over to give a gift to [other] recipients. // 74

16.207.s:
yatiścetprārthayellobhāddīyamānaṃ pratigraham ..
na tasya deyaṃ vidvadbhirna lobhaḥ śasyate yateḥ .. 75 ..
16.207.d:
यतिश्चेत्प्रार्थयेल्लोभाद्दीयमानं प्रतिग्रहम् ..
न तस्य देयं विद्वद्भिर्न लोभः शस्यते यतेः .. 75 ..
16.207.m: If an ascetic, out of greed, begs for an offering being given, / it should not be given to him by the wise; greed in an ascetic is not praised. // 75

16.207.s:
dhanaṃ prāpya yatirloke maunaṃ jñānaṃ ca nābhyaset ..
upabhogaṃ tu dānena jīvitaṃ brahmacaryayā .. 76 ..
16.207.d:
धनं प्राप्य यतिर्लोके मौनं ज्ञानं च नाभ्यसेत् ..
उपभोगं तु दानेन जीवितं ब्रह्मचर्यया .. 76 ..
16.207.m: An ascetic should not practice silence and knowledge in the world having acquired wealth, / nor worldly enjoyment through giving, nor a livelihood through celibacy. // 76

16.207.s:
kule janma ca dīkṣābhirye gatāste narottamāḥ..
saubhāgyamāpnuyālloke nūnaṃ rasavivarjanāt..77..
16.207.d:
कुले जन्म च दीक्षाभिर्ये गतास्ते नरोत्तमाः..
सौभाग्यमाप्नुयाल्लोके नूनं रसविवर्जनात्..77..
16.207.m: Those who have attained birth in a [noble] family and [proper] initiations are the best of men; / one certainly attains good fortune in the world by refraining from dainty foods. // 77

16.207.s: āyuṣmatyaḥ prajāḥ sarvā bhavantyāmiṣavarjanāt..78..
16.207.d: आयुष्मत्यः प्रजाः सर्वा भवन्त्यामिषवर्जनात्..78..
16.207.m: All one's offspring become long-lived by abstaining from meat. // 78

16.207.s:
cīravalkaladhṛktyaktvā vastrāṇyābharaṇāni ca..
nāgādhipatyaṃ prāpnoti upavāsena mānavaḥ..79..
16.207.d:
चीरवल्कलधृक्त्यक्त्वा वस्त्राण्याभरणानि च..
नागाधिपत्यं प्राप्नोति उपवासेन मानवः..79..
16.207.m: Discarding clothes and ornaments and wearing rags and bark, / a person attains lordship over serpents by fasting. // 79

16.207.s:
krīḍate satyavākyena svarge vai devataiḥ saha..
ahiṃsayā tathā''rogyaṃ dānātkīrtimanukramāt..7.1.207.80..
16.207.d:
क्रीडते सत्यवाक्येन स्वर्गे वै देवतैः सह..
अहिंसया तथा'ऽरोग्यं दानात्कीर्तिमनुक्रमात्..7.1.207.80..
16.207.m: By truthful speech one disports with the gods in heaven; / likewise, by non-violence one gains health, and by giving one gains fame in due order. // 80

16.207.s:
dvijaśuśrūṣayā rājyaṃ dvijatvaṃ cātipuṣkalam..
divyarūpamavāpnoti devaśuśrūṣayā naraḥ..81..
16.207.d:
द्विजशुश्रूषया राज्यं द्विजत्वं चातिपुष्कलम्..
दिव्यरूपमवाप्नोति देवशुश्रूषया नरः..81..
16.207.m: Through service to the twice-born a person attains kingship and bountiful brahminhood; / through service to the gods he attains a divine form. // 81

16.207.s:
annadānādbhavettṛptiḥ sarvakāmairanuttamaiḥ ..
dīpasya tu pradānena cakṣuṣmāñjāyate naraḥ .. 82 ..
16.207.d:
अन्नदानाद्भवेत्तृप्तिः सर्वकामैरनुत्तमैः ..
दीपस्य तु प्रदानेन चक्षुष्माञ्जायते नरः .. 82 ..
16.207.m: Satisfaction with all unsurpassed desires arises from the gift of food; / by the offering of a lamp, a person is born with good vision. // 82

16.207.s:
tuṣṭirbhavetsarvakālaṃ pradānādgandhamālyayoḥ ..
lavaṇasya tu dātārastilānāṃ sarpiṣastathā ..
tejasvino'pi jāyante bhoginaścirajīvinaḥ .. 83 ..
16.207.d:
तुष्टिर्भवेत्सर्वकालं प्रदानाद्गन्धमाल्ययोः ..
लवणस्य तु दातारस्तिलानां सर्पिषस्तथा ..
तेजस्विनोऽपि जायन्ते भोगिनश्चिरजीविनः .. 83 ..
16.207.m: Everlasting contentment comes from giving perfumes and garlands; / givers of salt, sesame seeds, and clarified butter / are born splendid, full of enjoyment, and long-lived. // 83

16.207.s:
sucitravastrābharaṇopadhānaṃ dadyānnaro yaḥ śayanaṃ dvijāya ..
rūpānvitāṃ pakṣmavatīṃ manojñāṃ bhāryāmarālopacitāṃ labhetsaḥ .. 84 ..
16.207.d:
सुचित्रवस्त्राभरणोपधानं दद्यान्नरो यः शयनं द्विजाय ..
रूपान्वितां पक्ष्मवतीं मनोज्ञां भार्यामरालोपचितां लभेत्सः .. 84 ..
16.207.m: The man who gives a twice-born a bed with cushions and colorful garments and ornaments / obtains an attractive wife endowed with beauty, fine eyelashes, and rich curly hair. // 84

16.207.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye śrāddhakalpe pātrāpātravicāravarṇanaṃnāma saptottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 207 ..
16.207.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये श्राद्धकल्पे पात्रापात्रविचारवर्णनंनाम सप्तोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 207 ..
16.207.m: Thus ends the two hundred and seventh chapter, entitled "Discussion of Worthy and Unworthy Recipients in the Rules of Śrāddha," in the first [part], the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, of the seventh [section], the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 207

16.208.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
idaṃ deyamidaṃ deyamiti proktaṃ tu yacchrutau ..
dānādānaviśeṣāṃstu śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ .. 1 ..
16.208.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
इदं देयमिदं देयमिति प्रोक्तं तु यच्छ्रुतौ ..
दानादानविशेषांस्तु श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः .. 1 ..
16.208.m: The Goddess said: / "'This should be given, this should be given,' as declared in the Veda— / I desire to hear the distinctions among gifts in truth. // 1

16.208.s:
kāni dānāni śastāni kasmai deyāni kānyapi ..
kālaṃ deśaṃ ca pātraṃ ca sarvamācakṣva me vibho .. 2 ..
16.208.d:
कानि दानानि शस्तानि कस्मै देयानि कान्यपि ..
कालं देशं च पात्रं च सर्वमाचक्ष्व मे विभो .. 2 ..
16.208.m: Which gifts are commended? And to whom should which gifts be given? / Declare to me, O Lord, everything regarding time, place, and recipient." // 2

16.208.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
vṛthā janmāni catvāri vṛthā dānāni ṣoḍaśa ..
sujanmāni ca catvāri mahādānāni ṣoḍaśa .. 3 ..
16.208.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
वृथा जन्मानि चत्वारि वृथा दानानि षोडश ..
सुजन्मानि च चत्वारि महादानानि षोडश .. 3 ..
16.208.m: Īśvara said: / "Useless births are four, and useless gifts are sixteen; / auspicious births are four, and great gifts are sixteen." // 3

16.208.s:
.. devyuvāca.. ..
etadvistarato brūhi devadevajagatpate .. 4 ..
16.208.d:
.. देव्युवाच.. ..
एतद्विस्तरतो ब्रूहि देवदेवजगत्पते .. 4 ..
16.208.m: The Goddess said: / "Speak of this in detail, O God of gods, Lord of the universe!" // 4

16.208.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
vṛthā janmāni catvāri yāni tāni nibodha me ..
kuputrāṇāṃ vṛthā janma ye ca dharmabahiṣkṛtāḥ ..
pravāsaṃ ye ca gacchaṃti paradāraratāḥ sadā .. 5 ..
16.208.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
वृथा जन्मानि चत्वारि यानि तानि निबोध मे ..
कुपुत्राणां वृथा जन्म ये च धर्मबहिष्कृताः ..
प्रवासं ये च गच्छंति परदाररताः सदा .. 5 ..
16.208.m: Īśvara said: / "Learn from me which the four useless births are: / useless is the birth of wicked sons and of those expelled from dharma, / and of those who go abroad, constantly devoted to other men's wives, // 5

16.208.s:
parapākaṃ ca ye'śnaṃti para dāraratāśca ye ..
apratyākhyaṃ vṛthā dānaṃ sadoṣaṃ ca tathā priye .. 6 ..
16.208.d:
परपाकं च येऽश्नंति पर दाररताश्च ये ..
अप्रत्याख्यं वृथा दानं सदोषं च तथा प्रिये .. 6 ..
16.208.m: and of those who eat food cooked by others and delight in other men's wives. / A gift that is irrevocable and flawed is also useless, O beloved! // 6

16.208.s:
ārūḍhapatite caiva anyāyopārjitaṃ dhanam ..
vṛthā brahmahane dānaṃ patite taskare tathā .. 7 ..
16.208.d:
आरूढपतिते चैव अन्यायोपार्जितं धनम् ..
वृथा ब्रह्महने दानं पतिते तस्करे तथा .. 7 ..
16.208.m: So too, wealth acquired unjustly given to one who has fallen from an ascetic vow, / a gift to a killer of a brahmin, to an outcaste, and likewise to a thief is useless; // 7

16.208.s:
guroścāprītijanane kṛtaghne grāmayājake ..
brahmabandhau ca yaddattaṃ yaddattaṃ vṛṣalīpatau .. 8 ..
16.208.d:
गुरोश्चाप्रीतिजनने कृतघ्ने ग्रामयाजके ..
ब्रह्मबन्धौ च यद्दत्तं यद्दत्तं वृषलीपतौ .. 8 ..
16.208.m: and what is given to one who causes displeasure to his guru, to an ungrateful person, to a village priest, / to a degraded brahmin, and what is given to the husband of a Śūdra woman; // 8

16.208.s:
vedavikrayiṇe caiva yasya copapatirgṛhe ..
strīnirjite ca yaddattaṃ vṛthādānāni ṣoḍaśa .. 9 ..
16.208.d:
वेदविक्रयिणे चैव यस्य चोपपतिर्गृहे ..
स्त्रीनिर्जिते च यद्दत्तं वृथादानानि षोडश .. 9 ..
16.208.m: and to a seller of the Veda, and to him in whose house there is a paramour, / and what is given to one conquered by a woman—these are the sixteen useless gifts. // 9

16.208.s:
sujanma ca suputrāṇāṃ ye ca dharme ratā narāḥ ..
pravāsaṃ na ca gacchaṃti paradāraparāṅmukhāḥ .. 7.1.208.10 ..
16.208.d:
सुजन्म च सुपुत्राणां ये च धर्मे रता नराः ..
प्रवासं न च गच्छंति परदारपराङ्मुखाः .. 7.1.208.10 ..
16.208.m: And auspicious is the birth of virtuous sons, and of men devoted to dharma, / who do not wander abroad, and who turn away from other men's wives. // 10

16.208.s:
gāvaḥ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ ratnāni ca sarasvatī ..
tilāḥ kanyā gajośvaśca śayyā vastraṃ tathā mahī .. 11 ..
16.208.d:
गावः सुवर्णं रजतं रत्नानि च सरस्वती ..
तिलाः कन्या गजोश्वश्च शय्या वस्त्रं तथा मही .. 11 ..
16.208.m: Cows, gold, silver, jewels, and Sarasvatī [i.e., books], / sesame seeds, a maiden, an elephant, a horse, a bed, clothing, and land, // 11

16.208.s:
dhānyaṃ payaśca cchatraṃ ca gṛhaṃ copaskarānvitam..
etānyeva mahādevi mahādānāni ṣoḍaśa .. 12 ..
16.208.d:
धान्यं पयश्च च्छत्रं च गृहं चोपस्करान्वितम्..
एतान्येव महादेवि महादानानि षोडश .. 12 ..
16.208.m: grain, milk, an umbrella, and a house furnished with utensils: / these indeed, O Great Goddess, are the sixteen great gifts. // 12

16.208.s:
garvāvṛtastu yo dadyādbhayātkrodhāttathaiva ca ..
bhuṃkte dānaphalaṃ taddhi garbhastho nātra saṃśaya .. 13 ..
16.208.d:
गर्वावृतस्तु यो दद्याद्भयात्क्रोधात्तथैव च ..
भुंक्ते दानफलं तद्धि गर्भस्थो नात्र संशय .. 13 ..
16.208.m: He who gives enveloped in pride, or out of fear, or out of anger, / enjoys the fruit of that gift while remaining in the womb; there is no doubt about this. // 13

16.208.s:
bālatve'pi ca so'śnāti yaddattaṃ daṃbhakāraṇāt ..
manyunā maṃtunā caiva tathaivārthasya kāraṇāt .. 14 ..
16.208.d:
बालत्वेऽपि च सोऽश्नाति यद्दत्तं दंभकारणात् ..
मन्युना मंतुना चैव तथैवार्थस्य कारणात् .. 14 ..
16.208.m: And he enjoys in childhood what was given on account of hypocrisy, / grief, or offense, and likewise for the sake of wealth. // 14

16.208.s:
deśe kāle ca pātre ca śuddhena manasā tathā ..
nyāyārjitaṃ ca yo dadyādyauvane sa tadaśnute .. 15 ..
16.208.d:
देशे काले च पात्रे च शुद्धेन मनसा तथा ..
न्यायार्जितं च यो दद्याद्यौवने स तदश्नुते .. 15 ..
16.208.m: He who gives justly acquired wealth with a pure mind, / in [the proper] place, time, and to a worthy recipient, enjoys it in youth. // 15

16.208.s:
anyāyenārjitaṃ dravyamapātre pratipāditam ..
kliṣṭaṃ ca vidhihīnaṃ ca vṛddhabhāve tadaśnute..16..
16.208.d:
अन्यायेनार्जितं द्रव्यमपात्रे प्रतिपादितम् ..
क्लिष्टं च विधिहीनं च वृद्धभावे तदश्नुते..16..
16.208.m: Wealth acquired unlawfully, presented to an unworthy recipient, / obtained with hardship, or devoid of proper rite—that he experiences in old age. (16)

16.208.s:
tasmāddeśe ca kāle ca supātre vidhinā naraḥ..
śubhārjitaṃ prayuñjīta śraddhayā śāṭhyavarjitaḥ.. 17..
16.208.d:
तस्माद्देशे च काले च सुपात्रे विधिना नरः..
शुभार्जितं प्रयुञ्जीत श्रद्धया शाठ्यवर्जितः.. 17..
16.208.m: Therefore, in the proper place and time, to a worthy recipient according to rule, / a man should give what was auspiciously acquired, with faith and free of deceit. (17)

16.208.s:
svādhyāyāḍhyaṃ yogavaṃtaṃ praśāṃtaṃ purāṇajñaṃ pāpabhīruṃ vadānyam..
strīṣu kṣāntaṃ dhārmikaṃ gośaraṇyaṃ vrataiḥ krāntaṃ tādṛśaṃ pātramāhuḥ..18..
16.208.d:
स्वाध्यायाढ्यं योगवंतं प्रशांतं पुराणज्ञं पापभीरुं वदान्यम्..
स्त्रीषु क्षान्तं धार्मिकं गोशरण्यं व्रतैः क्रान्तं तादृशं पात्रमाहुः..18..
16.208.m: Rich in Vedic study, endowed with yoga, peaceful, knowing the Purāṇas, fearing sin, generous, / patient with women, righteous, a protector of cows, steeped in vows—such a man they call a worthy recipient. (18)

16.208.s:
satyaṃ damastapaḥ śaucaṃ santoṣo'nairṣyamārjavam ..
jñānaṃ śamo dayā dānametatpātrasya lakṣaṇam .. 19 ..
16.208.d:
सत्यं दमस्तपः शौचं सन्तोषोऽनैर्ष्यमार्जवम् ..
ज्ञानं शमो दया दानमेतत्पात्रस्य लक्षणम् .. 19 ..
16.208.m: Truth, self-restraint, austerity, purity, contentment, absence of envy, uprightness, / knowledge, calm, compassion, charity—these are the characteristics of a worthy recipient. (19)

16.208.s:
evaṃvidhe tu yatpātre gāmekāṃ tu prayacchati ..
samānavatsāṃ kapilāṃ dhenuṃ sarvaguṇānvitām .. 7.1.208.20 ..
16.208.d:
एवंविधे तु यत्पात्रे गामेकां तु प्रयच्छति ..
समानवत्सां कपिलां धेनुं सर्वगुणान्विताम् .. 7.1.208.20 ..
16.208.m: When one gives even a single cow to such a worthy recipient— / a brown cow with a matching calf, endowed with all auspicious marks, (20)

16.208.s:
raupyapādāṃ svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ rudraloke mahīyate ..
ekāṃ gāṃ daśagurdadyādgośatī ca tathā daśa .. 21 ..
16.208.d:
रौप्यपादां स्वर्णशृङ्गीं रुद्रलोके महीयते ..
एकां गां दशगुर्दद्याद्गोशती च तथा दश .. 21 ..
16.208.m: with silver hooves and gold horns—he is glorified in the world of Rudra. / A master of ten cows should give one cow, and a master of a hundred cows likewise ten. (21)

16.208.s:
śataṃ sahasragurdadyātsarve samaphalāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
suśīlā somasaṃpannā taruṇī ca payasvinī ..
savatsā nyāyalabdhā ca pradeyā brāhmaṇāya gauḥ .. 22 ..
16.208.d:
शतं सहस्रगुर्दद्यात्सर्वे समफलाः स्मृताः ..
सुशीला सोमसंपन्ना तरुणी च पयस्विनी ..
सवत्सा न्यायलब्धा च प्रदेया ब्राह्मणाय गौः .. 22 ..
16.208.m: A master of a thousand cows should give a hundred; they are all held to have equal fruit. / Good-natured, beautiful, young, yielding milk, / with her calf and lawfully obtained—[such] a cow should be given to a brahmin. (22)

16.208.s:
vaṃdhyā sarogā hīnāṃgī duṣṭā vṛddhā mṛtaprajā ..
anyāyalabdhā dūrasthā nedṛśī gāṃ pradāpayet .. 23 ..
16.208.d:
वंध्या सरोगा हीनांगी दुष्टा वृद्धा मृतप्रजा ..
अन्यायलब्धा दूरस्था नेदृशी गां प्रदापयेत् .. 23 ..
16.208.m: Barren, diseased, deficient in limbs, vicious, aged, one whose offspring have died, / unlawfully acquired, or living far away—such a cow one should not give. (23)

16.208.s:
yo hīdṛśīṃ gāṃ dadāti devoddeśena mānavaḥ ..
pratyutādhogatiṃ yāti kliśyate ca maheśvari .. 24 ..
16.208.d:
यो हीदृशीं गां ददाति देवोद्देशेन मानवः ..
प्रत्युताधोगतिं याति क्लिश्यते च महेश्वरि .. 24 ..
16.208.m: For a man who gives such a cow dedicating it to a deity, / on the contrary goes to a downward state and suffers, O great goddess. (24)

16.208.s:
ruṣṭā kliṣṭā durbalā vyādhitā ca na dātavyā yā ca mūlyairadattaiḥ ..
leśo viprebhyo yayā jāyate vai tasyā dātuścāphalāḥ sarvalokāḥ .. 25 ..
16.208.d:
रुष्टा क्लिष्टा दुर्बला व्याधिता च न दातव्या या च मूल्यैरदत्तैः ..
लेशो विप्रेभ्यो यया जायते वै तस्या दातुश्चाफलाः सर्वलोकाः .. 25 ..
16.208.m: Angry, distressed, feeble, diseased, and acquired without paying the price—she should not be given; / if trouble arises for brahmins through her, all worlds are rendered fruitless for the giver. (25)

16.208.s:
atithaye praśāntāya sīdate cāhitāgnaye ..
śrotriyāya tathaikāpi dattā bahuguṇā bhavet .. 26 ..
16.208.d:
अतिथये प्रशान्ताय सीदते चाहिताग्नये ..
श्रोत्रियाय तथैकापि दत्ता बहुगुणा भवेत् .. 26 ..
16.208.m: To a peaceful guest who is in distress, who maintains the sacred fires, / and is learned in the Veda—even a single cow given becomes manifold. (26)

16.208.s:
gāṃ vikrīṇāti ceddevi brāhmaṇo jñānadurbalaḥ ..
nāsau praśasyate pātraṃ brāhmaṇo naiva sa smṛtaḥ .. 27 ..
16.208.d:
गां विक्रीणाति चेद्देवि ब्राह्मणो ज्ञानदुर्बलः ..
नासौ प्रशस्यते पात्रं ब्राह्मणो नैव स स्मृतः .. 27 ..
16.208.m: If a brahmin weak in knowledge sells the cow, O goddess, / he is not praised as a worthy recipient, nor indeed is he considered a brahmin. (27)

16.208.s:
bahubhyo na pradeyāni gaurgṛhaṃ śayanaṃ striyaḥ ..
vibhaktā dakṣiṇā hyeṣā dātāraṃ nopatiṣṭhati .. 28 ..
16.208.d:
बहुभ्यो न प्रदेयानि गौर्गृहं शयनं स्त्रियः ..
विभक्ता दक्षिणा ह्येषा दातारं नोपतिष्ठति .. 28 ..
16.208.m: A cow, a house, a bed, and women must not be given to many; / for this sacrificial gift, when divided, does not stand by the giver. (28)

16.208.s:
prāsādā yatra sauvarṇāḥ śayyā ravrojjvalāstathā ..
varāścāpsaraso yatra tatra gacchaṃti gopradāḥ .. 29 ..
16.208.d:
प्रासादा यत्र सौवर्णाः शय्या रव्रोज्ज्वलास्तथा ..
वराश्चाप्सरसो यत्र तत्र गच्छंति गोप्रदाः .. 29 ..
16.208.m: Where palaces are golden, and couches are bright as the sun, / and where there are excellent apsarases—there go the givers of cows. (29)

16.208.s:
nāsti bhūmisamaṃ dānaṃ nāsti gaṃgāsamā sarit ..
nāsti satyātparo dharmo nānyo devo maheśvarāt .. .. 7.1.208.30 ..
16.208.d:
नास्ति भूमिसमं दानं नास्ति गंगासमा सरित् ..
नास्ति सत्यात्परो धर्मो नान्यो देवो महेश्वरात् .. .. 7.1.208.30 ..
16.208.m: There is no gift equal to land; there is no river equal to the Gaṅgā; / there is no dharma higher than truth; there is no deity other than Maheśvara. (30)

16.208.s:
uccaiḥ pāṣāṇayuktā ca na samā naiva coṣarā ..
na nadīkūlavikaṭā bhūmirdeyā kadācana .. 31 ..
16.208.d:
उच्चैः पाषाणयुक्ता च न समा नैव चोषरा ..
न नदीकूलविकटा भूमिर्देया कदाचन .. 31 ..
16.208.m: High, full of stones, uneven, and salty barren ground, / or rugged land on riverbanks—such land should never be given. (31)

16.208.s:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi svarge vasati bhūmidaḥ ..
ācchettā cānumaṃtā ca tānyeva narakaṃ vrajet ..32..
16.208.d:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गे वसति भूमिदः ..
आच्छेत्ता चानुमंता च तान्येव नरकं व्रजेत् ..32..
16.208.m: The giver of land dwells in heaven for sixty thousand years; / the one who seizes it or approves of its seizure goes to hell for the very same period. (32)

16.208.s:
kurute puruṣaḥ pāpaṃ yatkiñcidvṛttikarśitaḥ ..
api gocarmamātreṇa bhūmidānena śuddhyati .. 33 ..
16.208.d:
कुरुते पुरुषः पापं यत्किञ्चिद्वृत्तिकर्शितः ..
अपि गोचर्ममात्रेण भूमिदानेन शुद्ध्यति .. 33 ..
16.208.m: Whatever sin a man commits when reduced to poverty in livelihood, / he is purified even by a gift of land measuring only a gocarma. (33)

16.208.s:
chatraṃ śayyāsanaṃ śaṃkho gajāśvāścāmarāḥ striyaḥ ..
bhūmiścaiṣāṃ pradānasya śivalokaḥ phalaṃ smṛtam .. 34 ..
16.208.d:
छत्रं शय्यासनं शंखो गजाश्वाश्चामराः स्त्रियः ..
भूमिश्चैषां प्रदानस्य शिवलोकः फलं स्मृतम् .. 34 ..
16.208.m: An umbrella, a bed and seat, a conch, elephants, horses, chowries, women, / and land: the world of Śiva is remembered as the fruit of giving these. (34)

16.208.s:
āditye'hani saṃkrāṃtau grahaṇe candra sūryayoḥ ..
pāraṇaiścaiva godāne nopoṣyaḥ pautravāngṛhī .. 35 ..
16.208.d:
आदित्येऽहनि संक्रांतौ ग्रहणे चन्द्र सूर्ययोः ..
पारणैश्चैव गोदाने नोपोष्यः पौत्रवान्गृही .. 35 ..
16.208.m: On a Sunday, on a saṃkrānti, during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, / on days of breaking a fast, and during the gift of a cow, a householder having grandsons should not fast. (35)

16.208.s:
indukṣaye tu saṃkrāntyāmekādaśyāṃ śate kṛte ..
upavāsaṃ na kurvīta yadīcchetsaṃtatiṃ dhruvam.. 36 ..
16.208.d:
इन्दुक्षये तु संक्रान्त्यामेकादश्यां शते कृते ..
उपवासं न कुर्वीत यदीच्छेत्संततिं ध्रुवम्.. 36 ..
16.208.m: At the disappearance of the moon, at a saṃkrānti, on the eleventh lunar day, and when a century [of fasts] is completed, / one should not observe a fast if he desires continuous lineage. (36)

16.208.s:
yathā śuklā tathā kṛṣṇā na viśeṣo'sti kaścana ..
tathāpi vardhate dharmaḥ śuklāyāmeva sarvadā .. 37 ..
16.208.d:
यथा शुक्ला तथा कृष्णा न विशेषोऽस्ति कश्चन ..
तथापि वर्धते धर्मः शुक्लायामेव सर्वदा .. 37 ..
16.208.m: As is the bright fortnight, so is the dark; there is no distinction whatsoever. / Nevertheless, merit always increases on the bright [fortnight] alone. (37)

16.208.s:
daśamyekādaśīviddhā dvādaśī ca kṣayaṃ gatā ..
naktaṃ tatra prakurvīta nopavāso vidhīyate .. 38 ..
16.208.d:
दशम्येकादशीविद्धा द्वादशी च क्षयं गता ..
नक्तं तत्र प्रकुर्वीत नोपवासो विधीयते .. 38 ..
16.208.m: When the eleventh day is touched by the tenth and the twelfth is diminished, / one should observe the night fast there; a complete fast is not prescribed. (38)

16.208.s:
upoṣyaikādaśīṃ yastu trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇam ..
karoti tasya naśyettu dvādaśa dadvādaśīphalam..39..
16.208.d:
उपोष्यैकादशीं यस्तु त्रयोदश्यां तु पारणम् ..
करोति तस्य नश्येत्तु द्वादश दद्वादशीफलम्..39..
16.208.m: He who fasts on the eleventh day and breaks the fast on the thirteenth / loses the fruit of the twelve dvādaśī [fasts]. (39)

16.208.s:
upavāse tathā śrāddhe na khādeddantadhāvanam..
dantānāṃ kāṣṭhasaṃgācca hanti saptakulāni vai..7.1.208.40..
16.208.d:
उपवासे तथा श्राद्धे न खादेद्दन्तधावनम्..
दन्तानां काष्ठसंगाच्च हन्ति सप्तकुलानि वै..7.1.208.40..
16.208.m: During a fast and at a śrāddha, one should not use a tooth-cleaning stick; / by contact of the teeth with wood, one destroys indeed seven generations. (40)

16.208.s:
darśaṃ ca paurṇamāsaṃ ca pituḥ sāṃvatsaraṃ dinam..
pūrvaviddhamakurvāṇo narakaṃ pratipadyate .. 41 ..
16.208.d:
दर्शं च पौर्णमासं च पितुः सांवत्सरं दिनम्..
पूर्वविद्धमकुर्वाणो नरकं प्रतिपद्यते .. 41 ..
16.208.m: The new moon, the full moon, and the annual day of one's father: / not performing them when overlapped by the previous day, one falls into hell. (41)

16.208.s:
hāniśca saṃtateḥ proktā daurbhāgyaṃ samavāpnuyāt ..
dravyābhāvetha śrāddhasya vidhiṃ vakṣyāmi tattvataḥ .. 42 ..
16.208.d:
हानिश्च संततेः प्रोक्ता दौर्भाग्यं समवाप्नुयात् ..
द्रव्याभावेथ श्राद्धस्य विधिं वक्ष्यामि तत्त्वतः .. 42 ..
16.208.m: And loss of offspring is declared; he would incur misfortune. / In the absence of wealth, I shall explain the rule of the śrāddha in truth: (42)

16.208.s:
ekenāpi hi vipreṇa ṣaṭpiṇḍaṃ śrāddhamācaret ..
ṣaḍarghyānpārayettatra tebhyo dadyādyathāvidhi .. 43 ..
16.208.d:
एकेनापि हि विप्रेण षट्पिण्डं श्राद्धमाचरेत् ..
षडर्घ्यान्पारयेत्तत्र तेभ्यो दद्याद्यथाविधि .. 43 ..
16.208.m: With even a single brahmin, one should perform the six-piṇḍa śrāddha; / one should offer six water offerings there and give to them according to rule. (43)

16.208.s:
pitā bhuṃkte dvija kare mukhe bhuṃkte pitāmahaḥ ..
prapitāmahastālusthaḥ kaṇṭhe mātāmahaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 44 ..
16.208.d:
पिता भुंक्ते द्विज करे मुखे भुंक्ते पितामहः ..
प्रपितामहस्तालुस्थः कण्ठे मातामहः स्मृतः .. 44 ..
16.208.m: The father eats in the brahmin's hand; the grandfather eats in his mouth; / the great-grandfather is in the palate; the maternal grandfather is held to be in the throat. (44)

16.208.s:
pramātāmahastu hṛdaye vṛddho nābhau tu saṃsthitaḥ ..
alābhe brāhmaṇasyaiva kuśaḥ kāryo dvijaḥ priye ..
idaṃ sarvapurāṇebhyaḥ sāramuddhatya cocyate .. 45 ..
16.208.d:
प्रमातामहस्तु हृदये वृद्धो नाभौ तु संस्थितः ..
अलाभे ब्राह्मणस्यैव कुशः कार्यो द्विजः प्रिये ..
इदं सर्वपुराणेभ्यः सारमुद्धत्य चोच्यते .. 45 ..
16.208.m: The maternal great-grandfather is in the heart, and the elder is established in the navel. / In the absence of a brahmin, dear lady, a brahmin should be made of kuśa grass. / This is declared having extracted the essence from all the Purāṇas. (45)

16.208.s:
na caitannāstike deyaṃ piśune vedanindake ..
prātaḥprātaridaṃ śrāvyaṃ pūjayitvā maheśvaram.. 46 ..
16.208.d:
न चैतन्नास्तिके देयं पिशुने वेदनिन्दके ..
प्रातःप्रातरिदं श्राव्यं पूजयित्वा महेश्वरम्.. 46 ..
16.208.m: And this must not be given to an atheist, a slanderer, or a reviler of the Vedas. / This should be recited morning after morning having worshipped Maheśvara. (46)

16.208.s:
kulīnaṃ sarvaśāstrajñaṃ yathā devaṃ maheśvaram ..
asya dharmasya vaktāraṃ chatraṃ dadyātprapūjayet .. 47 ..
16.208.d:
कुलीनं सर्वशास्त्रज्ञं यथा देवं महेश्वरम् ..
अस्य धर्मस्य वक्तारं छत्रं दद्यात्प्रपूजयेत् .. 47 ..
16.208.m: One should give an umbrella and worship the speaker of this dharma, / high-born and learned in all the scriptures, just like the god Maheśvara. (47)

16.208.s:
apūjyādvācakādyastu ślokamekaṃ śṛṇoti ca ..
nāsau puṇyamavāpnoti śāstracauraḥ smṛto hi saḥ .. 48 ..
16.208.d:
अपूज्याद्वाचकाद्यस्तु श्लोकमेकं शृणोति च ..
नासौ पुण्यमवाप्नोति शास्त्रचौरः स्मृतो हि सः .. 48 ..
16.208.m: He who hears even a single verse from an unworthy reader / does not attain merit; indeed, he is remembered as a thief of scripture. (48)

16.208.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjayedvācakaṃ budhaḥ ..
anyathā niṣphalaṃ tasya pustakaśravaṇaṃ bhavet.. 49 ..
16.208.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन पूजयेद्वाचकं बुधः ..
अन्यथा निष्फलं तस्य पुस्तकश्रवणं भवेत्.. 49 ..
16.208.m: Therefore, the wise person should worship the reciter with every effort. / Otherwise, his listening to the book will become fruitless. (49)

16.208.s:
yasyaiva tiṣṭhate gehe śāstrametatsadurlabham ..
tasya devi gṛhe tīrthaiḥ saha tiṣṭhecchivaḥ svayam .. 7.1.208.50 ..
16.208.d:
यस्यैव तिष्ठते गेहे शास्त्रमेतत्सदुर्लभम् ..
तस्य देवि गृहे तीर्थैः सह तिष्ठेच्छिवः स्वयम् .. 7.1.208.50 ..
16.208.m: In whose house this exceedingly rare treatise stays, / in his house, O goddess, Śiva himself dwells together with the sacred fords. (50)

16.208.s:
bahunātra kimuktena bhavenmokṣasya bhājanam ..
na caitatpiśune deyaṃ nāstike daṃbhasaṃyute . 51 ..
16.208.d:
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन भवेन्मोक्षस्य भाजनम् ..
न चैतत्पिशुने देयं नास्तिके दंभसंयुते . 51 ..
16.208.m: What is the use of speaking much here? He will become a vessel of liberation. / But this must not be given to a slanderer, an atheist, or one filled with hypocrisy. (51)

16.208.s: idaṃ śāntāya dāntāya deyaṃ śaivadvijanmane .. 52 ..
16.208.d: इदं शान्ताय दान्ताय देयं शैवद्विजन्मने .. 52 ..
16.208.m: This should be given to a peaceful, self-controlled, twice-born follower of Śiva. (52)

16.208.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye śrāddhakalpe dānapātrabrāhmaṇamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭottaradviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ .. 208 ..
16.208.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये श्राद्धकल्पे दानपात्रब्राह्मणमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामाष्टोत्तरद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः .. 208 ..
16.208.m: Thus ends the two-hundred-and-eighth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of a Brahmin as a Worthy Recipient of Gifts in the Rite of Śrāddha', in the First Prabhāsa-kṣetra-māhātmya, in the Seventh Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. (208)

16.209.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tato gacchenmahādevi mārkaṇḍeyeśamuttamam ..
tasmāduttaradigbhāge mārkaṇḍena pratiṣṭhitam ..1..
16.209.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ततो गच्छेन्महादेवि मार्कण्डेयेशमुत्तमम् ..
तस्मादुत्तरदिग्भागे मार्कण्डेन प्रतिष्ठितम् ..1..
16.209.m: Īśvara said: / Then, O great goddess, one should proceed to the supreme Mārkaṇḍeyeśa, / established in the northern direction from there by Mārkaṇḍeya. (1)

16.209.s:
sāvitryāḥ pūrvabhāge tu nātidūre vyavasthitam ..
maharṣirabhavatpūrvaṃ mārkaṇḍeya iti śrutaḥ .. 2 ..
16.209.d:
सावित्र्याः पूर्वभागे तु नातिदूरे व्यवस्थितम् ..
महर्षिरभवत्पूर्वं मार्कण्डेय इति श्रुतः .. 2 ..
16.209.m: It is situated not very far to the east of Sāvitrī. / In the past, there was a great seer known as Mārkaṇḍeya, (2)

16.209.s:
ajaraścāmaraścaiva prasādātpadmayoninaḥ ..
sa gatvā tatra viprendro devadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
liṃgaṃ tu sthāpayāmāsa jñātvā tatkṣetramuttamam .. 3 ..
16.209.d:
अजरश्चामरश्चैव प्रसादात्पद्मयोनिनः ..
स गत्वा तत्र विप्रेन्द्रो देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ..
लिंगं तु स्थापयामास ज्ञात्वा तत्क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् .. 3 ..
16.209.m: free from old age and immortal by the grace of the Lotus-born [Brahmā]. / Having gone there, that prince among brahmins established a liṅga / of the trident-bearing god of gods, knowing that field to be supreme. (3)

16.209.s:
sa taṃ pūjya vidhānena sthitvā dakṣiṇato muniḥ ..
padmāsanadharo bhūtvā dhyānāvasthastadā'bhavat .. 4 ..
16.209.d:
स तं पूज्य विधानेन स्थित्वा दक्षिणतो मुनिः ..
पद्मासनधरो भूत्वा ध्यानावस्थस्तदाऽभवत् .. 4 ..
16.209.m: Having worshipped it according to the injunctions and standing to the south, the sage, / adopting the lotus posture, then became absorbed in meditation.

16.209.s:
tasya dhyānaratasyaiva prayutānyarbudāni ca ..
yugānāṃ samatītāni na jānāti munīśvaraḥ .. 5 ..
16.209.d:
तस्य ध्यानरतस्यैव प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च ..
युगानां समतीतानि न जानाति मुनीश्वरः .. 5 ..
16.209.m: While he remained immersed in meditation, millions and billions / of yugas passed by; the lord of sages did not know [it].

16.209.s:
atha lopaṃ samāpannaḥ prāsādaḥ śāṃkaraḥ sthitaḥ ..
kālena mahatā devi pāṃsubhirmārutodbhavaiḥ .. 6 ..
16.209.d:
अथ लोपं समापन्नः प्रासादः शांकरः स्थितः ..
कालेन महता देवि पांसुभिर्मारुतोद्भवैः .. 6 ..
16.209.m: Then the temple belonging to Śaṅkara standing [there] fell into decay / over a long period of time, O goddess, [covered] by dust born of the wind.

16.209.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya prabuddho munisattamaḥ ..
apaśyatpāṃsubhirvyāptaṃ tatsarvaṃ śivamandiram .. 7 ..
16.209.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य प्रबुद्धो मुनिसत्तमः ..
अपश्यत्पांसुभिर्व्याप्तं तत्सर्वं शिवमन्दिरम् .. 7 ..
16.209.m: Then, after a certain time, the excellent sage awakened / and saw that entire temple of Śiva covered with dust.

16.209.s:
tataḥ kṛcchrātsa niṣkrāntaḥ khanitvā munipuṃgavaḥ ..
akarotsumahādvāraṃ pūjārthaṃ tasya bhāmini .. 8 ..
16.209.d:
ततः कृच्छ्रात्स निष्क्रान्तः खनित्वा मुनिपुंगवः ..
अकरोत्सुमहाद्वारं पूजार्थं तस्य भामिनि .. 8 ..
16.209.m: Then that best of sages, having dug his way out with difficulty, emerged / and made a great doorway for its worship, O lovely lady.

16.209.s:
praviśya tatra yo bhaktyā pūjayedvṛṣabhadhvajam ..
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ .. .. 9 ..
16.209.d:
प्रविश्य तत्र यो भक्त्या पूजयेद्वृषभध्वजम् ..
स याति परमं स्थानं यत्र देवो महेश्वरः .. .. 9 ..
16.209.m: Whoever enters there and worships the bull-bannered [god] with devotion / goes to the supreme abode where the divine Maheśvara dwells.

16.209.s:
devyuvāca ..
amaratvaṃ kathaṃ prāpto mārkaṃṇḍo munisattamaḥ ..
abhavatkautukaṃ hyetattasmāttvaṃ vaktumarhasi .. 7.1.209.10 ..
16.209.d:
देव्युवाच ..
अमरत्वं कथं प्राप्तो मार्कंण्डो मुनिसत्तमः ..
अभवत्कौतुकं ह्येतत्तस्मात्त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि .. 7.1.209.10 ..
16.209.m: The Goddess said: / How did the excellent sage Mārkaṇḍa attain immortality? / Indeed, curiosity has arisen in me regarding this; therefore, you ought to tell [me].

16.209.s:
amaratvaṃ yato nāsti prāṇināṃ bhuvi śaṃkara ..
devānāmapi kalpāṃte sa kathaṃ na mṛto muniḥ .. 11 ..
16.209.d:
अमरत्वं यतो नास्ति प्राणिनां भुवि शंकर ..
देवानामपि कल्पांते स कथं न मृतो मुनिः .. 11 ..
16.209.m: Since there is no immortality for living beings on earth, O Śaṅkara, / [and even] for the gods at the end of a kalpa, how is it that the sage did not die?

16.209.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
athātastvāṃ prava kṣyāmi yathāsāvamaro'bhavat ..
āsīnmuniḥ purākalpe mṛkaṇḍa iti viśrutaḥ .. 12 ..
16.209.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
अथातस्त्वां प्रव क्ष्यामि यथासावमरोऽभवत् ..
आसीन्मुनिः पुराकल्पे मृकण्ड इति विश्रुतः .. 12 ..
16.209.m: Īśvara said: / Now therefore I shall tell you how he became immortal. / In a previous kalpa there was a sage known as Mṛkaṇḍa.

16.209.s:
bhṛgoḥ putro mahābhāgaḥ sabhāryastapasi sthitaḥ ..
tasya putrastadā jāto vasatastu vanāṃtare .. 13 ..
16.209.d:
भृगोः पुत्रो महाभागः सभार्यस्तपसि स्थितः ..
तस्य पुत्रस्तदा जातो वसतस्तु वनांतरे .. 13 ..
16.209.m: He was the fortunate son of Bhṛgu, engaged in austerity together with his wife; / while he was dwelling within the forest, a son was then born to him.

16.209.s:
sa pāñcavārṣiko bhūtvā bāla eva guṇānvitaḥ ..
kasyacittvatha kālasya jñānī tatra samāgataḥ ..14..
16.209.d:
स पाञ्चवार्षिको भूत्वा बाल एव गुणान्वितः ..
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य ज्ञानी तत्र समागतः ..14..
16.209.m: He was a child of five years, endowed with good qualities; / then, after a certain time, an omniscient seer arrived there.

16.209.s:
tena dṛṣṭastadā bālaḥ prāṃgaṇe vicaranpriye ..
smṛtvā'hasacciraṃ kālaṃ bhāvyarthaṃ prati noditaḥ .. 15 ..
16.209.d:
तेन दृष्टस्तदा बालः प्रांगणे विचरन्प्रिये ..
स्मृत्वाऽहसच्चिरं कालं भाव्यर्थं प्रति नोदितः .. 15 ..
16.209.m: He then saw the boy wandering in the courtyard, O beloved, / and, recollecting [his fate], prompted regarding the future outcome, he laughed for a long time.

16.209.s:
tasya pitrā sa dṛṣṭastu sāmudrajño viduttamaḥ ..
hāsyasya kāraṇaṃ pṛṣṭo vismayānvitacetasā .. 16 ..
16.209.d:
तस्य पित्रा स दृष्टस्तु सामुद्रज्ञो विदुत्तमः ..
हास्यस्य कारणं पृष्टो विस्मयान्वितचेतसा .. 16 ..
16.209.m: He, the excellent scholar skilled in palmistry, was seen by the child's father, / and was asked the reason for his laughter with a mind filled with wonder:

16.209.s:
kasmānme sutamālokya smitaṃ vipra kṛtaṃ tvayā ..
tatra me kāraṇaṃ brahmanyathāvadvaktumarhasi .. .. 17 ..
16.209.d:
कस्मान्मे सुतमालोक्य स्मितं विप्र कृतं त्वया ..
तत्र मे कारणं ब्रह्मन्यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि .. .. 17 ..
16.209.m: "Why, O brahmin, having seen my son, did you smile? / You ought to tell me the reason for that properly, O holy one."

16.209.s: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā jñānī vipro vaco'bravīt .. 18 ..
16.209.d: इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ज्ञानी विप्रो वचोऽब्रवीत् .. 18 ..
16.209.m: Having heard his words, the wise brahmin spoke [these] words:

16.209.s:
ayaṃ putrastava mune sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutaḥ ..
adyaprabhṛti ṣaṇmāsamadhye mṛtyumavāpsyati .. 19 ..
16.209.d:
अयं पुत्रस्तव मुने सर्वलक्षणसंयुतः ..
अद्यप्रभृति षण्मासमध्ये मृत्युमवाप्स्यति .. 19 ..
16.209.m: "This son of yours, O sage, is endowed with all auspicious marks; / [yet] from today onward, within six months, he will meet his death.

16.209.s:
yadi jīvetpunarayaṃ cirāyurvai bhaviṣyati ..
ato mayā kṛtaṃ hāsyaṃ vicitrā karmaṇo gatiḥ .. 7.1.209.20 ..
16.209.d:
यदि जीवेत्पुनरयं चिरायुर्वै भविष्यति ..
अतो मया कृतं हास्यं विचित्रा कर्मणो गतिः .. 7.1.209.20 ..
16.209.m: If, however, he should survive, he will indeed be long-lived. / Therefore I laughed; wondrous is the course of karma!"

16.209.s:
etacchrutvā vaco raudraṃ jñāninā samudāhṛtam ..
vratopanayanaṃ cakre bālakasya pitā tadā .. 21 ..
16.209.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो रौद्रं ज्ञानिना समुदाहृतम् ..
व्रतोपनयनं चक्रे बालकस्य पिता तदा .. 21 ..
16.209.m: Having heard these terrible words spoken by the wise man, / the boy's father then performed the boy's investiture with the sacred thread.

16.209.s:
āha cainamṛṣiḥ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇamāgatam..
abhivādyāstrayo varṇāstataḥ śreyo hyavāpsyasi .. 22 ..
16.209.d:
आह चैनमृषिः पुत्रं दृष्ट्वा ब्राह्मणमागतम्..
अभिवाद्यास्त्रयो वर्णास्ततः श्रेयो ह्यवाप्स्यसि .. 22 ..
16.209.m: And the seer said to this son, upon seeing a brahmin who had arrived: / "The three varṇas are to be saluted [by you]; from that you will indeed attain welfare."

16.209.s:
evamuktaḥ sa vai vipraḥ karotyevābhivādanam ..
na varṇāvarajaṃ vetti bālabhāvādvarānane .. 23 ..
16.209.d:
एवमुक्तः स वै विप्रः करोत्येवाभिवादनम् ..
न वर्णावरजं वेत्ति बालभावाद्वरानने .. 23 ..
16.209.m: Having been instructed thus, the young brahmin continually offered salutations; / out of childishness, O fair-faced lady, he did not recognize one of inferior caste.

16.209.s:
paṃcamāsā hyatikrāntā divasāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ ..
etasminneva kāle tu prāptāḥ saptarṣayo'malāḥ .. 24 ..
16.209.d:
पंचमासा ह्यतिक्रान्ता दिवसाः पञ्चविंशतिः ..
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु प्राप्ताः सप्तर्षयोऽमलाः .. 24 ..
16.209.m: Five months and twenty-five days passed; / at that very time, the spotless Seven Seers arrived

16.209.s:
tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena tena mārgeṇa bhāmini ..
kālena tena sarve'tha yathāvadabhivādanaiḥ ..
āyuṣmānbhava tairuktaḥ sa bālo daṇḍavalkalī .. 25 ..
16.209.d:
तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगेन तेन मार्गेण भामिनि ..
कालेन तेन सर्वेऽथ यथावदभिवादनैः ..
आयुष्मान्भव तैरुक्तः स बालो दण्डवल्कली .. 25 ..
16.209.m: by that path in the course of a pilgrimage, O lovely lady. / At that time, through salutations performed properly [by him] / toward all [of them], that boy carrying a staff and wearing bark garments was told by them: "Be long-lived!"

16.209.s:
uktvā te tu punarbālaṃ vīkṣya vai kṣīṇajīvitam ..
dināni paṃca te hyāyurjñātvā bhītāstato'nṛtāt .. 26 ..
16.209.d:
उक्त्वा ते तु पुनर्बालं वीक्ष्य वै क्षीणजीवितम् ..
दिनानि पंच ते ह्यायुर्ज्ञात्वा भीतास्ततोऽनृतात् .. 26 ..
16.209.m: Having spoken, however, and looking at the boy whose life was exhausted, / knowing that his life was indeed five days [left], they were afraid of falsehood.

16.209.s:
brahmacāriṇamādāya gatāste brahmaṇo'ntike ..
pratimucyāgrato bālaṃ praṇemuste pitāmaham .. 27 ..
16.209.d:
ब्रह्मचारिणमादाय गतास्ते ब्रह्मणोऽन्तिके ..
प्रतिमुच्याग्रतो बालं प्रणेमुस्ते पितामहम् .. 27 ..
16.209.m: Taking the student of the Veda, they went to the presence of Brahmā; / setting down the boy before him, they bowed to the Grandfather.

16.209.s:
tatastenāpi bālena brahmā caivābhivāditaḥ ..
cirāyurbrahmaṇā bālaḥ prokto'sāvṛṣisannidhau .. 28 ..
16.209.d:
ततस्तेनापि बालेन ब्रह्मा चैवाभिवादितः ..
चिरायुर्ब्रह्मणा बालः प्रोक्तोऽसावृषिसन्निधौ .. 28 ..
16.209.m: Then Brahmā too was saluted by that boy; / in the presence of the seers, this boy was addressed by Brahmā: "Be long-lived!"

16.209.s:
tataste munayaḥ prītāḥ śrutvā vākyaṃ pitāmahāt ..
pitāmahastu tāndṛṣṭvā ṛṣīnprovāca vismitān ..
kena kāryeṇa vā''yātāḥ kena bālo niveditaḥ ..29..
16.209.d:
ततस्ते मुनयः प्रीताः श्रुत्वा वाक्यं पितामहात् ..
पितामहस्तु तान्दृष्ट्वा ऋषीन्प्रोवाच विस्मितान् ..
केन कार्येण वा'ऽयाताः केन बालो निवेदितः ..29..
16.209.m: Then those sages were pleased upon hearing the word from the Grandfather; / the Grandfather, however, seeing those amazed seers, said: / "For what purpose have you come, and why has this boy been presented?"

16.209.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
bhṛgoḥ putro mṛkaṇḍastu kṣīṇāyustasya bālakaḥ ..
akālena pitā jñātvā babaṃdhāsya ca mekhalām .. 7.1.209.30 ..
16.209.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
भृगोः पुत्रो मृकण्डस्तु क्षीणायुस्तस्य बालकः ..
अकालेन पिता ज्ञात्वा बबंधास्य च मेखलाम् .. 7.1.209.30 ..
16.209.m: The seers said: / "Mṛkaṇḍa is the son of Bhṛgu, and his boy has a short lifespan; / knowing this untimely [death], his father bound the girdle upon him.

16.209.s:
yajñopavītaṃ ca tatastena vipreṇa bodhitaḥ ..
yaṃ kañciddrakṣyase loke bhramantaṃ bhūtale dvijam .. 31 ..
16.209.d:
यज्ञोपवीतं च ततस्तेन विप्रेण बोधितः ..
यं कञ्चिद्द्रक्ष्यसे लोके भ्रमन्तं भूतले द्विजम् .. 31 ..
16.209.m: And [he gave him] the sacred thread; then he was instructed by that brahmin: / 'Whatever twice-born you see wandering anywhere on earth,

16.209.s:
tasyābhivādanaṃ kāryaṃ nityameva ca putraka ..
tato vayamanenaiva dṛṣṭā bālena sattama .. .. 32 ..
16.209.d:
तस्याभिवादनं कार्यं नित्यमेव च पुत्रक ..
ततो वयमनेनैव दृष्टा बालेन सत्तम .. .. 32 ..
16.209.m: a salutation must always be made to him, O son.' / Then we were seen by this very boy, O best of beings,

16.209.s:
tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena daivayogātpitāmaha ..
